headline: Fort Bragg Has Bet the Farm on 2026 and There Is No Going Back
body:
I need to lay out exactly what Harrison Bragg has done this offseason because I am not sure everyone in this league understands the scale of it.

Fort Bragg has traded away four 2027 draft picks. The 2nd rounder went to Doob's Agency. The 3rd went to Chicago Zestiest Man in the London deal. The 5th went to Pakistan Bombers. The 7th went to Beer. That is four selections out of fourteen gone. Bragg has 10 picks left in next year's draft and nothing in rounds 2, 3, 5, or 7.

He also shipped out Quinshon Judkins, Jordan Addison, TreVeyon Henderson, RJ Harvey, Emeka Egbuka, Darnell Mooney, and Odell Beckham Jr. over the last two weeks. In return he brought in Drake London, Javonte Williams, Woody Marks, Kendre Miller, Tre Tucker, and Gunnar Helm. London is the centerpiece. Everything else is support.

The receiver room is now Drake London, Mike Evans, DJ Moore, Rashod Bateman, and Tre Tucker. Jacobs and Pollard at running back are steady. Andrews at tight end is proven. Three quarterbacks remains a problem I have been complaining about for weeks and Bragg still will not fix it.

If this team wins the championship, Bragg is a genius who went back to back and cemented a dynasty. If this team goes 6-7 and misses the playoffs, he just mortgaged two years of draft capital for nothing. He burned the boats on the beach. Now he has to conquer or drown.

The Bombers continue to get stronger without giving up anything meaningful. Najee Harris joined Robinson and Jeanty at running back. Nacua and Smith lead the receivers. Hurts and Daniels at quarterback. This team added a starting NFL running back off the waiver wire while Fort Bragg was trading picks to acquire the same caliber of player. That is the difference between a roster built right on draft day and one that has to scramble to catch up.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: Post-Trade Power Rankings: The Model Sees Four Tiers and Beer Is the Biggest Surprise
body:
Tier 1 - Championship contenders (projected 9+ wins):

Pakistan Bombers at 10.4 wins. Robinson, Jeanty, Harris at RB. Nacua, Smith, Flowers at WR. Hurts and Daniels at QB. Championship probability: 24.1%.

I Heart Gingers at 9.8 wins. Chase, Higgins, Diggs at receiver. Brown, Stevenson, Dobbins at RB. LaPorta and Kittle at TE. Single-QB vulnerability (Love only) is the one flaw.

Doob's Agency at 9.3 wins. Burrow and Goff at QB. Barkley and Walker at RB. McMillan, Watson, Kupp, Allen, Deebo, Pittman - seven viable receivers is the deepest group in the league. Tyler Warren as the only TE remains the one risk.

Tier 2 - Playoff contenders (projected 7-8 wins):

Beer/Pavel Dorofeyev at 8.1 wins. Biggest mover since draft day. Stafford and Stroud at QB. Williams, Judkins, Montgomery at RB. St. Brown, Harrison Jr., McConkey at WR. Three tight ends in Fannin, Goedert, and Dulcich. Complete roster built entirely through trades.

Englewood Ninjas at 7.9 wins. Taylor, JSN, Waddle, Bowers. Clean construction.

Mount Olympus at 7.8 wins. McCaffrey and Hall when healthy are elite. Deep receiver room.

The Vile Horrendous at 7.5 wins. Cook, Love, Wilson, Nabers, Odunze. Youngest core in the league with six RBs and six WRs.

Fort Bragg at 7.3 wins. London, Evans, Moore, Jacobs, Andrews. But three QBs waste two bench spots and four missing 2027 picks leave zero margin for error.

VancouverPantiesDeJarome at 7.1 wins. Lamar, Achane, Lamb, Metcalf is a top-4 starting core. Three total running backs is the thinnest depth in the league.

Tier 3 - Bubble (projected 5-6 wins):

Pluto Shraazinatorz at 6.2 wins. Allen is elite. Henry is aging. Jones and Ferguson were nice trade adds. WR depth behind Collins and Pickens is thin.

The Watermark at 5.1 wins. Gibbs is top-3 and nothing else projects above replacement level. Calvin Ridley was cut for Kayshon Boutte, who has 11 career NFL receptions. Four tight ends. Six receivers who project to a combined weekly total lower than Puka Nacua alone. This roster got worse since the last time I wrote about it.

Tier 4 - Rebuilding (projected under 5 wins):

Nabers In Paris at 4.2 wins. Three QBs, two kickers, five wasted roster spots. Irving and Hubbard helped at RB but the construction remains inefficient.

Chicago Zestiest Man at 3.8 wins. One rookie QB (Dart). Got Henderson, Harvey, Addison, Egbuka, and a 3rd round pick from the London trade. Solid rebuild haul but the present-day roster has no proven QB or RB1. McBride is the best player here.

Amon Ra Dawgin at 3.4 wins. No defense. No kicker. One QB. Jefferson and Adams wasted on an incomplete roster.
author: Maya Chen

headline: The Watermark Just Cut Calvin Ridley for Kayshon Boutte and I Need Answers
body:
The Watermark dropped Calvin Ridley - a receiver with 400 career NFL catches - and picked up Kayshon Boutte from the Patriots. KAYSHON BOUTTE. A man with 11 career receptions. Eleven. I have more receptions at my family Thanksgiving football game.

Preston Schneider's receiver room is now Chris Olave, Wan'Dale Robinson, De'Zhaun Stribling, Jalen McMillan, Jauan Jennings, and Kayshon Boutte. Six receivers and I would not start five of them. Gibbs is out there running for 25 points a week and the rest of this roster is working against him. Four tight ends. SIX mediocre receivers. Zero trades made to improve. I do not understand.

Now let me talk about what IS working.

Miles Hughes is the most improved manager of the offseason. Beer went from a joke roster with seven running backs to Stafford and Stroud at QB, Williams and Judkins and Montgomery at RB, St. Brown and Harrison Jr. and McConkey at WR. That man executed a full roster rebuild through trades alone. Respect.

Fort Bragg and Chicago completed the biggest trade of the offseason. Bragg got Drake London alongside Evans and Moore. Chicago got Henderson, Harvey, Addison, Egbuka, and a 3rd round pick. Bragg went all-in on 2026. Ehrig is clearly building for 2027 with those young pieces and the extra draft capital. Both approaches make sense for where each team is.

Chicago now has four running backs in Tuten, Mason, Harvey, and Henderson. None of them are proven RB1s but Henderson and Harvey both have paths to starting jobs on their NFL teams. If either one breaks out this roster suddenly looks a lot different than the bottom-of-the-barrel projection everyone is giving it. Do not sleep on Zach Ehrig just because he traded London. That 3rd round pick from Fort Bragg plus his own full set of 2027 picks means he is set up for a strong draft next year.

And AMON RA DAWGIN. Andrew. Please. The season starts in 27 DAYS. No defense. No kicker. One quarterback. Jefferson and Adams are going to put up 40 combined and you are going to lose by 12 because two lineup slots are posting zeroes. PICK UP A DEFENSE.
author: DeShawn "Showtime" Harris

headline: The Three Offseason Strategies That Will Define the 2026 Season
body:
Every franchise chose a path this offseason. Let me break down the three approaches and who executed each one best.

Strategy 1: The All-In. Fort Bragg is the textbook case. Bragg traded four future picks, shipped seven players, and reshaped his roster around London, Evans, Moore, Jacobs, and Andrews. The 2027 draft will have no 2nd, 3rd, 5th, or 7th round pick. If this team does not make a deep playoff run, the rebuild will be painful. But Bragg has a trophy. He knows what winning requires. The roster talent is there. The concern is the three-quarterback inefficiency and the lack of depth at running back beyond Jacobs and Pollard. Williams and Marks from the Chicago trade help, but Kendre Miller is unproven and the margin for injury is thin.

Strategy 2: The Rebuild Through Trades. Beer and Chicago both chose this path from different directions. Hughes entered the draft with seven running backs and a plan nobody understood. Two weeks later he has Stafford, Stroud, Williams, Judkins, Montgomery, St. Brown, Harrison Jr., McConkey, Fannin, Goedert, and Dulcich. That is a complete roster at every position built entirely through phone calls and negotiation. Ehrig traded London for four young players and a draft pick, accepting a harder 2026 in exchange for a better 2027. Henderson and Harvey both have breakout potential. Addison and Egbuka provide immediate depth. The 3rd round pick from Fort Bragg gives him extra draft capital next year. The question for Ehrig is whether Dart can hold the quarterback position together long enough for the young pieces to develop. If he can, this rebuild was smart. If he cannot, Chicago is looking at another bottom-three finish.

Strategy 3: The Stand Pat. The Watermark and Amon Ra Dawgin both chose inaction, and both are worse for it. Schneider cut Ridley for Boutte this week, which is not an improvement. Four tight ends remain. No trades have been made to address the WR2 void or the running back depth behind Gibbs. Grossman has had weeks to add a defense and kicker and has not done it. Both rosters have elite individual talent surrounded by incomplete construction. The league is not waiting for them.

Claire's Verdict: The manager who positioned himself best is Miles Hughes. He identified a strategy on draft day, executed it through multiple trades, and emerged with a roster that went from the league's worst to a legitimate playoff contender. The manager who needs to act most urgently is Andrew Grossman. Three waiver wire transactions would transform his team's outlook. There is no excuse for entering September without a defense, a kicker, and a backup quarterback.
author: Claire Westbrook

headline: The Watermark Just Replaced Calvin Ridley With a Man Who Has Eleven Career Catches and I Am Running Out of Ways to Be Subtle
body:
I have been doing this job all offseason. I have been professional. I have been restrained. I have used phrases like "certain teams in the West" and "aquatic-themed franchises." I have been the picture of journalistic integrity.

I cannot do it anymore.

The Watermark dropped Calvin Ridley and replaced him with Kayshon Boutte, who has been in the NFL for two years and has fewer catches than I have fingers. The receiver room is now Chris Olave and five guys whose combined career stats would not fill a tweet. And there are STILL four tight ends on the roster. Four. In a league that starts one. This is like watching someone put four spare tires in the trunk and then drive on three flat ones.

ANYWAY. Positive news.

Miles Hughes is a certified genius and I owe him a public apology. I made fun of him for weeks. I compared him to a squirrel. I questioned his understanding of fantasy football. And then he turned those seven running backs into Stafford, McConkey, Judkins, and the most dramatic roster transformation I have ever witnessed. Beer is dead. Pavel Dorofeyev lives. And Marvin Harrison Jr. is finally starting.

Fort Bragg completed the London trade with Chicago and now has London, Evans, and Moore at receiver, which is terrifying. But Bragg still has three quarterbacks and traded away four draft picks. That roster is a sports car with no spare tire and no insurance.

Chicago got four young players and a 3rd round pick for London, which honestly is not bad for a team that was going nowhere anyway. Henderson and Harvey could both be starting running backs by October. Addison is a real NFL receiver. Egbuka is playing for Tom Brady. Zach Ehrig took a bad hand and played it about as well as anyone could.

Also Andrew Grossman still does not have a defense or a kicker. At this point I think someone should physically go to his house, open his laptop, navigate to ESPN, and press the buttons for him. This is an intervention-level situation. Andrew, please. I believe in you.
author: Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini

headline: Builders, Gamblers, and the Ones Who Stood Still
body:
Twenty-seven days before the season opens, the MFGA looks nothing like it did when the draft ended. Fourteen rosters went through the same two weeks. Not all of them came out the same way.

Miles Hughes built something. That is the simplest way to describe what happened with Beer over the last fourteen days. He walked into the draft with seven running backs that looked like a mistake. Then, one phone call at a time, he converted those pieces into the roster he actually wanted. Stafford. McConkey. Judkins. Each trade a step in a sequence only Hughes could see. By the time the last deal closed, the team that every analyst dismissed had Amon-Ra St. Brown and Marvin Harrison Jr. in its starting lineup with three viable tight ends on the bench. The draft was never the destination. It was the supply run.

Harrison Bragg gambled. The defending champion looked at a roster that won it all and decided it was not enough to win again. So he traded four picks. Shipped seven players. Acquired Drake London and created a receiver room with Evans and Moore that opposing managers will lose sleep over. The trade with Chicago was the headline, but the real story is the 2027 draft board with four empty rows. Bragg is spending the future on a single season the way a poker player pushes all their chips to the center and waits for the cards to turn.

Zach Ehrig made the hardest choice. He traded his best player knowing full well what the group chat would say. London was the one name on his roster that commanded respect. Trading him for Henderson, Harvey, Addison, Egbuka, and a future pick was not a surrender. It was a decision to stop pretending a one-star roster could compete and start building something that might actually work in 2027. The rebuild will not be comfortable. Dart at quarterback is a gamble. The running back room is young and unproven. But the 3rd round pick from Fort Bragg, combined with his own full draft next year, gives him the capital to restock properly. Sometimes the bravest thing a manager can do is admit that this is not their year.

And then there are the ones who stood still. Preston Schneider cut Calvin Ridley and added Kayshon Boutte. Andrew Grossman has Justin Jefferson and two empty starting slots. Both rosters have the kind of singular talent that wins individual weeks but loses seasons when the structure around it is hollow.

There is a window in every offseason where change is possible. Some managers walked through it and came out stronger. Some are still standing outside, watching, telling themselves there is still time. There is still time. But there is less of it than there was yesterday. And the league remembers who moved and who did not.
author: Valentina Rojas

headline: Five Draft Picks Gone. Josh Jacobs Facing Suspension. And Harrison Bragg Is Still Trading.
body:
I have been covering this league for three years. I have never seen a franchise bet this aggressively on a single season. And I am starting to think it is going to backfire.

Fort Bragg just sent a 4th round pick and Woody Marks to The Vile Horrendous for MarShawn Lloyd. That is the fifth 2027 draft pick Harrison Bragg has traded away this offseason. Fifth. The 2nd went to Doob's Agency. The 3rd went to Chicago. The 4th just went to The Vile Horrendous. The 5th went to Pakistan Bombers. The 7th went to Beer. Fort Bragg now has NINE picks in next year's draft instead of fourteen, with nothing in rounds 2, 3, 4, 5, or 7. That is not aggressive roster management. That is a man setting his house on fire to stay warm.

And here is the part that makes it worse. Josh Jacobs is not just dealing with a groin injury that kept him out of training camp for nearly three weeks. He has been charged with battery and criminal damage to property stemming from a domestic incident in May. The NFL is actively investigating whether to suspend him. ESPN's Adam Schefter has confirmed the league is reviewing disciplinary action. If Jacobs gets even a two-game suspension, Fort Bragg is starting Tony Pollard and MarShawn Lloyd at running back in Weeks 1 and 2. Lloyd has played in ONE NFL game in two seasons due to injuries. He has carried the ball six times in his professional career. Six.

Bragg also picked up Chris Brooks from Green Bay's roster, which tells you everything about how worried he is. Brooks is a pass-blocking specialist who rushed for 106 yards on 27 carries all of last season. That is not a running back. That is an offensive lineman who sometimes holds the football.

Meanwhile, Lucas Fawcett and the Pakistan Bombers quietly scooped up Kaleb Johnson off the waiver wire today after the Steelers traded him to Green Bay. Johnson was a third-round pick in 2025 who flopped in Pittsburgh - 28 carries, 69 yards, 2.5 yards per carry. But he ran for 1,537 yards and 21 touchdowns at Iowa. In Green Bay's offense with Jacobs potentially missing time, Johnson could see real volume. And Fawcett grabbed him for free while Bragg spent a draft pick on Lloyd. That is the difference between these two franchises right now.

headline: Correction: It Was Six Picks, Not Five. And That Makes It Worse.
body:
Three days ago I wrote that Harrison Bragg had traded away five 2027 draft picks. I wrote that the MarShawn Lloyd deal cost him a 4th rounder. I wrote that Fort Bragg had nine picks left and nothing in rounds 2, 3, 4, 5, or 7.

All three of those numbers were wrong.

I have been wrong before. Not often, but it happens, and when it happens I say so in print instead of quietly hoping nobody pulls up the draft board. So here it is.

The Lloyd trade did not cost Fort Bragg a 4th. It cost a 6th and an 11th. Two picks, not one. Bragg still has his 2027 4th rounder sitting exactly where it was, and that is the only part of this correction that works in his favor.

Everything else works against him. Count it properly and Harrison Bragg has traded away SIX 2027 draft picks this offseason, not five. The 2nd went to Doob's Agency. The 3rd went to Chicago Zestiest Man. The 5th went to Pakistan Bombers. The 6th and the 11th both went to The Vile Horrendous. The 7th went to Beer. Six selections out of fourteen, gone.

Fort Bragg walks into next year's draft with eight picks. A keeper, a 4th, an 8th, a 9th, a 10th, a 12th, a 13th, and a 14th. Nothing in the second. Nothing in the third. Nothing in the fifth, sixth, seventh, or eleventh. That is not a draft board. That is a receipt.

So I got the round wrong. I did not get the story wrong. If anything I undersold it. I said this was a man setting his house on fire to stay warm, and it turns out there was one more room burning than I counted.

Josh Jacobs is still under league review. MarShawn Lloyd has still played one NFL game in two seasons. Tony Pollard is still the contingency plan. None of that changed because I miscounted a round number, and none of it gets any easier for Fort Bragg in Week 1.

Get the details right, Hammer. I will. Bragg should too.

CORRECTION: My August 30 story, "Five Draft Picks Gone. Josh Jacobs Facing Suspension. And Harrison Bragg Is Still Trading.", reported that Fort Bragg sent its 2027 4th round pick to The Vile Horrendous in the MarShawn Lloyd trade, that five picks had been dealt, and that Fort Bragg held nine 2027 selections. The trade actually sent the 2027 6th and 11th round picks. Six picks have been traded, Fort Bragg holds eight, and the 4th rounder is still theirs. The league draft board has been updated. The error was mine.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: GAME DAY BURN: The Book of Jobe, Chapter One
body:
Vibe check: three quarters of dogshit football, then a fourth quarter that turned into a live-streamed mugging. New England led 10-0 and had this thing by the throat. Then Drake Maye threw three picks AND ate three sacks in twelve minutes of game clock, and a man whose last name is pronounced Job finished him off in the back of the end zone.

I pulled the ESPN play-by-play AND everybody's Week 1 lineups, because half the fun is who left points rotting on the bench.

JAXON SMITH-NJIGBA: 8 catches, 122 yards, 1 TD on 11 targets. 26.20. Started at WR by Englewood (Drew).

Nobody was within twelve of him. And the part the recaps skipped: the 45-yard touchdown that tied it 10-10 is logged as pass SHORT LEFT. Lock threw a five-yard dig and JSN ran the other 40 through the entire Patriots secondary. That was not a bomb, dawg. That was a grown man deciding he was done being polite.

Eleven targets on a night his starting QB got hurt on the first drive. Drew squeezed a WR1 ceiling out of DREW LOCK. Filthy.

RHAMONDRE STEVENSON: 18 carries, 51 yards, plus 5 grabs for 44. 14.50. Started at RB by I Heart Gingers (Carter).

2.8 a carry is miserable, but he caught five balls and PPR does not care how ugly it looked. Carter got RB2 money out of a guy running like his cleats were on backwards.

SEAHAWKS D/ST: 10 allowed, 3 sacks, 3 picks. 14.00. Started by Fort Bragg (Harrison).

Three DIFFERENT guys got the picks - Pritchett (30-yard return), Julian Love, and Jobe. Harrison will spend all week talking like he scouted this instead of clicking a defense on Saturday.

DRAKE MAYE: 23/33, 178 yards, 1 TD, 3 INT, plus 7 carries for 47. 9.82. Started at QB by Starving Ethiopians (Stephen).

His legs are the only reason that number has a 9 in front of it. The arm went full Old Testament.

Maye spent the fourth quarter getting Job'd. Deep ball intended for Romeo Doubs, picked at the SEA 3. Deep middle to DeMario Douglas, picked at the NE 47. Three sacks in between. Everything stripped away one piece at a time and no explanation offered.

Then the ending, which gets funnier every rewatch. New England drove to the Seattle 16 with 26 seconds left. That is a 34-yard field goal to tie and Borregales had already banged one in from 50. Instead Maye chucked it deep right into the end zone at Mack Hollins and JOSH JOBE toe-tapped the son of a bitch for the pick. Pronounced Job. God is real and He has a sense of humor.

And Jobe was not a cameo. He is on FOUR of New England's last six snaps - dropped Larison, dropped Maye on a scramble, shoved Hollins out at the 16, then took the ball. Not a plot twist. That is one guy running every plague himself.

JADARIAN PRICE: 10 carries, 52 yards, 2 catches. 7.80. Started at RB by The Watermark (Preston).

5.2 a pop, most efficient back on the grass, and nobody will mention it. Preston, real flex piece.

JASON MYERS: 2/2, from 30 and the go-ahead 26, plus the XP. 7.00. Started at K by Carter.

Boring, unsexy, decisive. Kicker points are like winning an argument by staying awake longest.

STUD OF THE NIGHT: Jaxon Smith-Njigba, 26.20. Best player on the field with a backup quarterback feeding him.

DICK OF THE DAY: ROMEO DOUBS. Three targets, ZERO catches, 0.00 points, and one of those targets got housed at the 3-yard line. Here is the beautiful part - Carter had him on the BENCH. So Doubs put up a fat nothing, got his own QB intercepted, and the only manager he screwed was Stephen, whose team he is not even on. Sabotaged a franchise from outside the building. Incredible work.

BENCH CRIMES: Matt left Cooper Kupp (5.50) AND George Holani (2.90) on the bench and started the Patriots defense and a kicker instead. That is 8.4 points in the closet, my guy. Drew started Rashid Shaheed in the FLEX for 1.40 and benched AJ Barner (3.30), a self-own he can afford after a 27-point night. Preston benched Corey Kiner (1.10), worth exactly what he cost.

INJURY REPORT: SAM DARNOLD got his hip wrecked on a Dre'Mont Jones sack at 12:27 of the first quarter and never came back. 1/2 for 13 yards, 0.52 points, ESPN has him Questionable. AND LIAM HAD HIM ON THE BENCH. The one week Liam benches his backup QB, that QB gets folded in half on the opening drive. Accidental genius. Doesn't matter, Liam still scored a clean 0.00 off this game and starts the week in a hole.

Also TREVEYON HENDERSON was listed OUT and played zero snaps. Zach had him benched anyway, so nothing was lost except Zach's will to live.

SCOREBOARD CHECK, started players only: Drew 27.60, Harrison 14.00 head-to-head. Carter 21.50, Liam 0.00. Stephen 15.42, Lucas 0. Preston 13.40, Miles 0 - Miles's only guy here was Charbonnet on IR, a hell of a way to participate. Matt 13.00 against an Evan roster with nobody in the game. Andrew and Zach tied at nothing, same for Shreyus and Josh P.

LOOKING AHEAD: THURSDAY NIGHT AT THE MCG

49ers at Rams, Melbourne Cricket Ground, 8:35 Eastern, on Netflix. The Rams are the home team in Australia. Sure. And I checked everybody's Thursday lineups. Nobody wins a matchup tonight - Sunday and Monday are still coming - this is just who grabs the lead going in.

THE MAIN EVENT: Miles versus Preston is a full Rams civil war and both men have committed. Miles is STARTING Matthew Stafford, Kyren Williams, AND Harrison Mevis. Preston is STARTING the Rams D/ST. Same broadcast, opposite directions - every Stafford touchdown pays Miles and takes a bite out of Preston's defense. Miles is at a flat zero and down 13.40, so this is his shot to flip that before Sunday. Load-bearing Stafford. Terrifying.

Liam is starting Christian McCaffrey and needs him to go nuclear, because he is down 21.50. Good news: Carter BENCHED George Kittle, so Carter cannot score tonight even if Kittle catches four touchdowns. Liam gets a free swing at that hole, though Carter's roster wakes right back up Sunday.

Lucas is starting Puka Nacua and needs 15.42 to pass Stephen. Puka does that on two drives. And Stephen BENCHED Blake Corum, so he is frozen at 15.42 until Sunday. Lucas can take the lead tonight and make Stephen sit on it for three days, which is its own kind of torture.

Drew starts Brock Purdy and Eddy Pineiro, two 49ers, up 13.60 already. Harrison counters with Davante Adams and genuinely needs him to be 2021 Davante Adams. Andrew is starting Mike Evans in a 0-0 matchup, so one Evans touchdown puts him up on Zach. Least earned lead in league history, and it will not survive the weekend. Matt BENCHED Deebo Samuel Sr., so his 13.00 just sits there and vibes until Sunday.

Then Sunday, all fourteen rosters at once, plus Monday night to settle it, and everybody finds out what they actually built in August. Set your damn lineups.
author: JoJo Martinez

headline: GAME DAY BURN: Mad Matt and the Fury Road to the One-Yard Line
body:
Vibe check: 100,021 Australians paid actual money to walk into the Melbourne Cricket Ground and watch the Los Angeles Rams get dragged behind a truck for three hours. They came for football. They got Mad Max: Fury Road, except the road is 100 yards long and the Rams ran out of gas at the one.

Rams led 7-3 in the second quarter. Then San Francisco scored 24 straight. 49ers 27, Rams 7. And the Rams were the designated HOME team, by the way. Imagine flying 10,000 miles to get booed in your own building. They could have done that at SoFi.

I pulled the ESPN play-by-play AND everybody's Thursday lineups, because the lineup card is where the real crimes are.

BROCK PURDY: 25/34, 205 yards, 3 TD, 1 INT, plus 5 carries for 29. 21.10. Started at QB by Englewood (Drew).

Three touchdowns to THREE different guys - Demarcus Robinson from 39, Mike Evans from 2, Deebo from 15. Purdy spread it around like a man tipping every bartender in the place. 205 yards is not a big number and he did not need it to be. Efficient, boring, lethal. The Toyota Camry of quarterbacks, and the Camry just lapped you.

KYREN WILLIAMS: 11 carries, 41 yards, 1 TD, plus 3 grabs for 24. 15.50. Started at RB by Pavel Dorofeyev (Miles).

3.7 a carry and the only Ram to reach the end zone all night. Punched it in from 5 at 14:57 of the second, which was the last time anybody in Los Angeles felt good about anything.

EDDY PINEIRO: 2/3, from 20 and a 56-YARD BOMB, plus 3/3 on extra points. 10.00. Started at K by Drew.

Ten points from a kicker. He also doinked a 52-yarder off the RIGHT UPRIGHT in the fourth, which is the field goal equivalent of a dart hitting the wire and bouncing back into your beer.

MIKE EVANS: 6 catches, 49 yards, 1 TD on 7 targets. 16.90. Started at WR by Amon Ra Dawgin (Andrew).

Andrew needed exactly one Evans touchdown to take a lead he did not earn. He got it on a 2-yard throw at 11:03 of the third. Called his shot and the shot was two feet long.

CHRISTIAN McCAFFREY: 10 carries, 68 yards, plus 5 catches for 20 on 8 targets. 13.80. Started at RB by Mount Olympus (Liam).

6.8 a carry, 88 total yards, and ZERO touchdowns, because every time San Francisco reached the goal line Purdy threw it to somebody else. Liam needed nuclear. He got a space heater.

PUKA NACUA: 5 catches, 74 yards on 9 targets. 12.40. Started at WR by Pakistan Bombers (Lucas).

Nine targets and a 41-yard catch that set up the only Rams touchdown, and one enormous problem: Lucas needed 15.42 to pass Stephen. Puka got 12.40. THREE POINT OH TWO SHORT. He was projected 21.04, so before anybody goes digging through Lucas's bench for a villain, understand that this was not a lineup problem. This was a Puka problem.

MATTHEW STAFFORD: 15/25, 155 yards, ZERO TD, 1 INT, and 2 carries for MINUS ONE YARD. 4.10. Started at QB by Miles.

Projected 17.49. Delivered 4.10. That is a 13.39-point crater, the widest gap between expectation and reality anywhere on that field. Last week I wrote "load-bearing Stafford, terrifying." The load was not borne, dawg. Four point one.

And now the play that decided this game and will get shown in Melbourne pubs for ten years. Third quarter, Rams go 12 plays and 72 yards, eating SEVEN MINUTES AND TWENTY-TWO SECONDS of clock, all the way to 4th and Goal at the San Francisco ONE. Down 17-7. And the call is... Matthew Stafford, right guard, keep it himself. OSA ODIGHIZUWA met him in the hole and put him in the dirt for no gain. Replay official reviewed it. UPHELD. Seven and a half minutes of football for zero points, like assembling IKEA furniture all afternoon and ending up with a stool that will not stand.

Then San Francisco took over at their own 1 and went NINETY-NINE YARDS in 11 plays. Ninety-nine. The Rams handed them the ball on the doorstep and the 49ers walked it the entire length of a cricket ground and scored. A 14-point swing inside twelve minutes, and the game died at the bottom of it.

Four separate Rams possessions ended inside 49ers territory with nothing: two turnovers on downs, a Tyler Higbee fumble that FRED WARNER punched out and Keion White scooped at the 43, and a Stafford interception. Warner finished with 11 tackles and a forced fumble and spent the night living in the Rams backfield like he was paying rent.

DAVANTE ADAMS: 3 catches, 26 yards on 6 targets. 5.60. Started at WR by Fort Bragg (Harrison).

I said Harrison needed 2021 Davante Adams. He got 2026 Davante Adams, which is a guy who ran six routes and caught three of them for the yardage of one decent run play. Projected 13.82. Delivered a third of it.

STUD OF THE NIGHT: Brock Purdy, 21.10 against a 15.48 projection, three touchdowns to three different receivers. Nobody else in this game was that efficient, and Drew paired him with his own kicker for 31.10 in a single night.

Except the highest score in this entire game did not belong to Purdy. It belonged to a man sitting on a BENCH. So let us talk about that.

DICK OF THE DAY: MATT GINGRICH. Not a player. The manager. DEEBO SAMUEL SR. went 6 catches, 48 yards, a 15-yard touchdown, a 12-yard carry, AND a 45-yard kick return that set up another touchdown. EIGHTEEN POINTS. THE HIGHEST TOTAL OF ANY PLAYER IN THIS GAME. And Matt had him on the bench.

And before anybody says the projections let him off the hook, they do not. Deebo's 18.00 beat every single starter Matt could have swapped him for: Tetairoa McMillan (14.81), Kenneth Walker III in the FLEX (14.70), Michael Pittman Jr. (12.31). Not one of them was projected to reach what Deebo actually did. I warned him in this exact column last week - I wrote that Matt BENCHED Deebo so his 13.00 would just sit there and vibe until Sunday. He read it, or he did not, and either way Deebo put up 18 in a jersey Matt was not wearing. That is leaving a winning lottery ticket in your jeans and running the wash. Matt still leads Evan 13.00 to nothing, which is the only mercy in this paragraph.

Dishonorable mention to HARRISON MEVIS, projected 9.41, scored 1.00, because his offense never got him close enough to attempt a single field goal. One extra point all night. A kicker with one attempt is a DJ who got to play one song before the power went out.

INJURY REPORT: DAVIS ALLEN took one to the head on a 13-yard catch in the third, came back, and is Questionable. KAM CURL is Questionable with an ankle. NATE LANDMAN and KEVIN DOTSON both got dinged late. KONATA MUMPFIELD got hurt and returned inside of two minutes, the fastest anything happened for Los Angeles all night. On the 49ers side, JAKE TONGES went down with a knee and DE'ZHAUN STRIBLING with an ankle, both Questionable, neither on anybody's roster in this league, so nobody here has to pretend to care.

Special mention to JORDAN WHITTINGTON, who returned 4 kickoffs for 94 yards and also FUMBLED one before recovering his own mess at the 27. Sir. This is the Melbourne Cricket Ground. Have some dignity.

And STETSON BENNETT came in for the last drive, went 2/3 with a 9-yard scramble, and marched the Rams to the San Francisco 13 before the clock hit zero. A garbage-time drive to nowhere against a defense that had already showered. The football equivalent of texting an apology at 4am.

SCOREBOARD CHECK, Week 1, started players only, through Thursday night:

Drew 58.70, Harrison 19.60. Drew added 31.10 in one night off Purdy and Pineiro and now owns the highest total in the league by 37 points. Harrison got 5.60 of Davante Adams and a bad feeling.

Miles 20.60, Preston 14.40. MILES FLIPPED IT. He sat at a flat zero and down 13.40 when I wrote about him last week, he started three Rams in a game the Rams lost by 20, his quarterback missed his projection by 13.39, and he STILL took the lead. Kyren carried Stafford's corpse across the line.

Carter 21.50, Liam 13.80. Carter did not score a single point Thursday and gained ground anyway.

Andrew 16.90, Zach 0. One Mike Evans touchdown, and Zach has to sit there and look at it.

Stephen 15.42, Lucas 12.40. Stephen has not scored a point since Wednesday and is still ahead, purely because Puka Nacua came up 8.64 short of what he was supposed to do.

Matt 13.00, Evan 0. Matt's lead is intact and his best player watched the whole thing in a polo shirt.

Shreyus 0, Josh P 0. Two teams, zero players in the game, a perfect nothing. Pluto vs Vancouver remains the most respectful matchup on the slate.

LOOKING AHEAD: SUNDAY, ALL AT ONCE

That is the appetizer finished. Thursday gave us one game and a Rams funeral. Sunday gives us the entire NFL at once, every roster in this league live at the same time, and Monday night to settle whatever is left standing.

Nobody has won anything yet. Drew's 58.70 looks enormous right now and it is one bad Sunday from being a normal score. Lucas is 3.02 behind a man who cannot score again until Sunday, which is its own special torture: nothing to fix, nobody to blame, just a wide receiver who owes him nine points. Preston needs his actual skill players, because his defense gave him one point and a migraine. Zach, Evan, Shreyus and Josh P are all sitting on zeros with their entire season still ahead of them, which is either optimism or denial depending on what their rosters look like.

Set your damn lineups. Check them twice. Ask Matt Gingrich what happens when you don't.

headline: MATCHUP BURN: Seven Games, Seven Funerals, 350 Points on the Bench
body:
Vibe check: fourteen rosters went live at the same time and seven of them got dragged into the parking lot. Preston hung 165.66, the highest number anybody put up all week. Harrison, the DEFENDING CHAMPION, managed 65.52 and finished dead last while Patrick Mahomes watched from his bench in street clothes.

Biggest blowout: Shreyus by 57.80. Closest game: Matt by 6.80. And this league left 350.70 points on its collective bench, which is its own kind of crime scene.

THE LOSERS

HARRISON BRAGG, Fort Bragg Confederates. 65.52. Lost to Drew 98.30. Margin 32.78.

Sixty-five points. From the guy wearing the crown. Lowest score in the league and it is not close.

KYLER MURRAY: MINUS 0.38. Negative. Projected 16.40. A quarterback in a PPR league finished the week owing his team money. That stat line is offensive in ways the FCC would fine me for.

Then it gets worse, because PATRICK MAHOMES put up 21.66 ON THE BENCH. Swap him in for Kyler and that is a 22.04-point swing by itself. DJ MOORE: 21.00, also benched, while Harrison started DRAKE LONDON (5.50), DAVANTE ADAMS (5.60), and TONY POLLARD in the flex for 4.40.

His optimal lineup was 110.76. He scored 65.52. That is 45.24 points in the closet and 59.2% roster efficiency, dead last in the league. He did not lose this game. He forfeited it and then showed up anyway.

Rick "The Hammer" Dalton spent the offseason screaming that Fort Bragg traded away six 2027 picks to go all-in on this season. Week 1 return on that investment: last place and a quarterback with negative points.

JOSH P, VancouverPantiesDeJarome. 76.86. Lost to Shreyus 134.66. Margin 57.80.

Got absolutely bent over. KYLE PITTS SR.: 0.00, projected 9.83. TITANS D/ST: MINUS 1.00. KENNY GAINWELL in the flex: 2.80 on a 12.03 projection. BRANDON AUBREY: 2.00. Four starters, 3.80 points combined.

Lamar Jackson went 24.96 and CeeDee Lamb 15.40 and it did not matter, because the back half of that lineup showed up to a gunfight with a pool noodle.

BENCH CRIME: PARKER WASHINGTON went 19.30 in a polo shirt. Vikings D/ST 5.00 while the Titans went negative. Dalton Schultz 7.50 while Pitts laid an egg. Thirty points left behind.

Maya Chen's model had Vancouver in Tier 2 at 7.1 projected wins with "a top-4 starting core." The model did not account for Kyle Pitts being Kyle Pitts.

STEPHEN CERQUONE, Starving Ethiopians. 92.82. Lost to Lucas 139.42. Margin 46.60.

Chuba Hubbard 23.70 and Bucky Irving 20.30 showed up. Nobody else did. DRAKE MAYE: 9.82, the second straight week I have had to write about Drake Maye getting Job'd.

Here is the part that should keep Stephen awake. BRYCE YOUNG scored 31.44 ON THE BENCH. MALIK WILLIS scored 16.70, ALSO ON THE BENCH. He owns three quarterbacks, started the worst one, and the gap between Young and Maye alone was 21.62.

A.J. BROWN: 5.60. TERRY McLAURIN: 3.40. Two of the receivers Stephen got back from Lucas in the Puka Nacua trade Rick called a fleecing in August. They combined for 9.00 against Puka's 12.40 for the guy who just beat him by 46. Aging like milk in a hot car.

MILES HUGHES, Pavel Dorofeyev. 113.50. Lost to Preston 165.66. Margin 52.16.

You can score 113 and still get rolled. MATTHEW STAFFORD: 4.10 on a 17.50 projection. Third time I have written that number. Load-bearing Stafford collapsed and everybody saw it coming, including me, in print, twice.

C.J. STROUD: 16.46 ON THE BENCH. DALLAS GOEDERT: 23.70 ON THE BENCH while HAROLD FANNIN JR. started for 4.10. Miles left 37.56 home. David Montgomery 28.90 and Amon-Ra St. Brown 28.70 bought him nothing, because his quarterback and tight end combined for 8.20.

CARTER COLE, I Heart Gingers. 87.28. Lost to Liam 105.10. Margin 17.82.

JA'MARR CHASE: 3.20. Projected 19.95. If that performance was a Tinder date you would block the number and change cities.

MATTHEW GOLDEN 15.50 and STEFON DIGGS 15.50 both sat watching Chase catch nothing. Bench Chase for Golden, that is 12.30. Bench J.K. Dobbins in the flex (3.60) for Diggs, another 11.90. Carter wins this game by six.

Maya had I Heart Gingers in Tier 1 at 9.8 projected wins on "Chase, Higgins, Diggs at receiver." The two he started, Chase and Tee Higgins (8.90), combined for 12.10. The third was on his bench. Tier 1, my guy.

EVAN BROCKWAY, The Vile Horrendous. 100.26. Lost to Matt 107.06. Margin 6.80.

Most painful loss in the league and entirely self-inflicted. JALEN COKER: 33.80. BENCHED. ISAIAH LIKELY: 27.80. BENCHED.

He lost by 6.80 with sixty-one points of production in the closet. Coker was the highest scorer on any bench in this league. Evan started ROME ODUNZE (7.20) and TRAVIS KELCE (10.10) instead. Swap either and he wins going away. Optimal 144.56, actual 100.26, 44.30 left behind in a game decided by less than seven. Absolute poverty decision-making on a fine roster.

ZACH EHRIG, Chicago Zestiest Man. 122.30. Lost to Andrew 137.70. Margin 15.40.

Highest-scoring loser in the league, and he deserves a hug right up until you look at his flex. JORDAN ADDISON: 0.00, projected 9.91. Started. DEVAUGHN VELE: 19.90. Benched.

One swap. That is the whole game. Vele for Addison and Zach wins by 4.50. Jaxson Dart went 26.60, Trey McBride 24.50, Steelers D/ST 19.00, and one empty flex spot cost him the week.

THE WINNERS

MATT GINGRICH, Doob's Agency. 107.06 over Evan's 100.26. Congratulations, you did not win this game. Evan lost it for you.

KENNETH WALKER III went 34.10 in the flex, carrying a lineup where SAQUON BARKLEY managed 9.00 and JOE BURROW 14.16 on an 18.15 projection. And Matt is back in this column for the same crime as last week: CHRISTIAN WATSON 32.70 and DEEBO SAMUEL SR. 18.00, both benched, one week after I dedicated a Dick of the Day to exactly this. He left 36.98 home and won anyway. Luckiest 1-0 in the league.

ANDREW GROSSMAN, Amon Ra Dawgin. 137.70 over Zach's 122.30.

Cleanest win of the week. JUSTIN JEFFERSON 31.20, TREVOR LAWRENCE 26.10, JAVONTE WILLIAMS 24.20, DALTON KINCAID 18.00, MIKE EVANS 16.90. Five starters in double digits and all five beat their projections. Only 9.30 left on the bench, 93.7% efficiency, second best in the league. No notes.

LIAM HUGHES, Mount Olympus. 105.10 over Carter's 87.28.

Won ugly. CHRISTIAN McCAFFREY went 13.80 and his CHIEFS D/ST outscored him at 14.00. KYLE MONANGAI 20.40, PAT FREIERMUTH 15.60, and CALEB DOUGLAS 14.40 all sat, 24.20 left behind in a game he won by 17.82. Rick predicted Liam would LOSE this one, so the win counts.

DREW FLYNN, Englewood Ninjas. 98.30 over Harrison's 65.52.

JAXON SMITH-NJIGBA 26.20, JONATHAN TAYLOR 25.10, and BROCK PURDY 21.10 did all of it: 72.40 from three men and 25.90 from the other six. JAYLEN WADDLE 1.20, CHARGERS D/ST 0.00, RASHID SHAHEED 1.40 in the flex. Drew won by 33 with three starters combining for 2.60, which tells you everything about what Harrison did.

LUCAS FAWCETT, Pakistan Bombers. 139.42 over Stephen's 92.82.

ASHTON JEANTY 32.70 and BIJAN ROBINSON 31.30. Sixty-four points from the backfield Rick called the best this league has ever seen, and for one week The Hammer looks like a prophet. ZAY FLOWERS 26.00 and JALEN HURTS 24.72 finished it.

But COLSTON LOVELAND went 0.00 and the TEXANS D/ST went MINUS 4.00. Lucas won by 46 with two starters actively subtracting from his total. PUKA NACUA also went 12.40 on a 21.05 projection, second straight week Puka has undersold his price tag.

PRESTON SCHNEIDER, The Watermark. 165.66 over Miles's 113.50.

Highest score in the league and the best-managed roster of the week. CALEB WILLIAMS: 37.26 on a 16.39 projection. JAHMYR GIBBS: 33.60. D'ANDRE SWIFT: 32.40 in the flex on a 12.31 projection. CHRIS OLAVE: 28.20. Four starters over 28 points.

Maya had The Watermark in Tier 3, "bubble," 5.1 projected wins, and wrote that six of his receivers "project to a combined weekly total lower than Puka Nacua alone." Olave by himself more than doubled Puka's 12.40. Tommy Mancini spent August mocking the Kayshon Boutte signing. Boutte scored 3.10 and Preston BENCHED him, because Preston, unlike Tommy, can read a depth chart. Only 4.70 left behind, best efficiency in the league at 97.2%.

SHREYUS SAXENA, Pluto Shraazinatorz. 134.66 over Josh P's 76.86.

JOSH ALLEN 35.66 and DERRICK HENRY 35.30, both roughly DOUBLE their projections. Seventy-one points from two guys, and Rick had Pluto losing this game. The part nobody will mention: CAMERON DICKER 2.00, JAKE FERGUSON 2.60, GEORGE PICKENS 5.80, three starters for 10.40, and JUWAN JOHNSON scored 14.40 on the bench while Ferguson stunk.

WEEKLY AWARDS

PLAYER OF THE WEEK: CALEB WILLIAMS, 37.26. Projected 16.39, more than doubled it, highest single score by any player on any roster in this league, started or benched.

BUST OF THE WEEK: KYLER MURRAY, MINUS 0.38 against a 16.40 projection. A 16.78-point crater and the only starting quarterback in the league to finish in the red.

MANAGER OF THE WEEK: PRESTON SCHNEIDER. League-high 165.66, only 4.70 left on the bench, 97.2% of his ceiling, and he benched the exact guys who deserved benching. Flawless.

CLOWN OF THE WEEK: HARRISON BRAGG. 45.24 points left on the bench and 59.2% efficiency, dead last in both. Mahomes (21.66) and DJ Moore (21.00) watched a 32-point loss that his optimal lineup wins 110.76 to 98.30. The defending champion lost this game in the lineup screen. Dishonorable mention: EVAN BROCKWAY, who left 44.30 behind and lost by 6.80. Harrison left more. Evan's actually mattered.

BLOWOUT OF THE WEEK: Shreyus 134.66 over Josh P 76.86. Margin 57.80.

NAIL BITER OF THE WEEK: Matt 107.06 over Evan 100.26. Margin 6.80, the only single-digit game on the slate.

STAT LINE OF THE WEEK: TEXANS D/ST, MINUS 4.00, started by the guy who won by 46. Lucas put a defense in his lineup that played so badly it took four points OFF the board and he still cruised. That unit scored fewer points than my dead grandma's fantasy team and she doesn't have WiFi in heaven.

UPDATED STANDINGS

EAST
1. Pakistan Bombers (Lucas) 1-0, 139.42
2. Mount Olympus (Liam) 1-0, 105.10
3. Chicago Zestiest Man (Zach) 0-1, 122.30
4. Pavel Dorofeyev (Miles) 0-1, 113.50
5. The Vile Horrendous (Evan) 0-1, 100.26
6. Starving Ethiopians (Stephen) 0-1, 92.82
7. Fort Bragg Confederates (Harrison) 0-1, 65.52

WEST
1. The Watermark (Preston) 1-0, 165.66
2. Amon Ra Dawgin (Andrew) 1-0, 137.70
3. Pluto Shraazinatorz (Shreyus) 1-0, 134.66
4. Doob's Agency (Matt) 1-0, 107.06
5. Englewood Ninjas (Drew) 1-0, 98.30
6. I Heart Gingers (Carter) 0-1, 87.28
7. VancouverPantiesDeJarome (Josh P) 0-1, 76.86

The West went 5-2 and owns three of the top five scores. The East has Lucas and a bread line.

LOOKING AHEAD: WEEK 2

FORT BRAGG (0-1) at STARVING ETHIOPIANS (0-1). Two teams that scored 65.52 and 92.82 and both know it. Harrison needs to start Mahomes, which sounds obvious because it is. Stephen needs Bryce Young in after 31.44 on the bench. Whoever fixes their quarterback first wins, and Rick predicted Stephen takes this one. THE WATERMARK (1-0) at THE VILE HORRENDOUS (0-1). Preston rolls in off 165.66 with Caleb Williams, Gibbs, and Swift all cooking. Evan has the talent to hang, he scored 100.26 with 44.30 on the bench, but he has to actually start Coker (33.80) and Likely (27.80) this time. PICK: Preston, until Evan shows me he can fill out a roster.

ENGLEWOOD NINJAS (1-0) at I HEART GINGERS (0-1). Drew won with three starters who combined for 2.60, so there is more here than the score says. Carter needs Chase to remember he is Ja'Marr Chase after 3.20, and Golden and Diggs in the lineup instead of on the pine. PICK: Carter. Chase does not put up 3.20 twice, and Waddle plus the Chargers defense cannot both be that bad again.

PLUTO SHRAAZINATORZ (1-0) at AMON RA DAWGIN (1-0). Best matchup on the board, both undefeated, second and third in league scoring. Josh Allen (35.66) and Derrick Henry (35.30) against Justin Jefferson (31.20) and Trevor Lawrence (26.10). Shreyus needs Pickens (5.80) and Ferguson (2.60) to be real players. Andrew needs nothing. DOOB'S AGENCY (1-0) at CHICAGO ZESTIEST MAN (0-1). The luckiest team in the league visiting the unluckiest. Zach needs to fill his flex with a human being. Matt needs to start Watson (32.70) and Deebo (18.00) before I lose my mind. PICK: Zach, and if Matt benches Watson again I am dedicating the entire column to him.

PAKISTAN BOMBERS (1-0) at VANCOUVERPANTIESDEJAROME (0-1). Lucas brings Jeanty and Bijan against the lowest score in the West. Josh P needs Achane (10.60) and Metcalf (8.00) to wake up, and he needs to bench Kyle Pitts into the sun. Rick actually predicted Vancouver wins this one back in August. PICK: Lucas, comfortably. That backfield put up 64 on its own and Josh P's whole roster managed 76.86.

MOUNT OLYMPUS (1-0) at PAVEL DOROFEYEV (0-1). Liam won ugly with 24.20 on the bench. Miles scored 113.50 and got blown out anyway. Miles needs Stafford (4.10 on a 17.50 projection) benched for Stroud (16.46), and Goedert (23.70) in over Fannin (4.10). PICK: Miles, but only if he benches Stafford. If Stafford starts, Liam by 20.

Fourteen teams, one week down, and the story of Week 1 is not talent. It is that this league left 350.70 points on the bench and four of the seven losers lost by less than they left behind. Set your damn lineups. Ask Harrison what happens when you don't.
author: JoJo Martinez

headline: Fawcett Robbed This League Once Already. Grossman Just Let Him Do It Again.
body:
Let me be absolutely clear about what just happened. Lucas Fawcett walked into a second trade negotiation this calendar year and walked out holding the best player in the deal. Again. In August he sent A.J. Brown, Terry McLaurin and Aaron Jones to Nabers In Paris and came back with Puka Nacua, and I called that a fleecing at the time. Tonight he sent Kaelon Black and Alec Pierce to Amon Ra Dawgin and came back with Mike Evans, Denzel Boston and a 2027 10th round pick. Three assets out of that side of the table, two bench players in.

Here is the part that should end the argument. Every one of those four players was on a roster in Week 1, so you do not have to project anything. Mike Evans scored 16.90 and started for Amon Ra. Denzel Boston scored 13.90 and sat on Amon Ra's bench. Kaelon Black scored 8.00 on the Bombers bench. Alec Pierce scored 10.10 on the Bombers bench. Grossman shipped out 30.80 points of production and brought back 18.10. He also threw in a draft pick to make sure the math got worse.

I wrote in August that Pakistan Bombers built a war machine and nobody in this league was ready. Week 1 they put up 139.42 and beat Nabers by 46. Their answer to being the best roster in the MFGA was to go get another receiver. That is not complacency. That is a manager who understands that the only thing standing between him and a title is a bad week, and he is buying insurance against bad weeks in bulk.

Now let me give you the one thing that gives me pause, because I am not in the business of pretending a trade is perfect when it is not. The Bombers now have three running backs. Three. Ashton Jeanty, Bijan Robinson and Kaleb Johnson, who has not scored a point. Fawcett just traded away his fourth back to add his eighth receiver. If Jeanty or Robinson misses time, that roster has nothing behind them and eight wideouts who cannot carry the ball. That is a real risk and I am not going to paper over it.

It is still a robbery. I have been wrong before. Not often, but it happens. This is not one of those times. Pakistan Bombers won this trade the moment Grossman picked up the phone.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: The Evans Trade by the Numbers: The Gap Is Narrower Than You Think, and It Is Still a Loss
body:
The reaction to this trade has been loud, so let me put actual numbers against it, because the raw production gap and the projection gap tell two different stories and both are worth understanding.

Start with what happened in Week 1. Amon Ra sent out Mike Evans, who scored 16.90, and Denzel Boston, who scored 13.90 on the bench. Amon Ra received Alec Pierce, who scored 10.10, and Kaelon Black, who scored 8.00, both from the Bombers bench. That is 30.80 out and 18.10 in, a 12.70 point deficit against one week of results.

Now run it against projections instead, which is the fairer test because one week of receiving production is mostly noise. Evans was projected 10.65 and Boston 8.28, a combined 18.93. Pierce was projected 9.70 and Black 4.50, a combined 14.20. On a projection basis the weekly gap is 4.73, not 12.70. Evans beat his projection by 6.25 on Thursday night in Melbourne and that single game is doing most of the work in how this deal is being described.

But the projection math is also where the real problem shows up, and it is not about talent. It is about roster slots. Evans was a starter for Amon Ra in Week 1. Pierce and Black are, on current construction, not. Grossman already rostered six running backs before this trade and he still rosters six now, because Black replaced Nicholas Singleton. His receiver room went from seven bodies to five, and the two he gave up were his second and fourth highest scorers at the position. You cannot start a sixth running back. Points that cannot enter a lineup have a value of zero regardless of what the projection says.

The one asset nobody is pricing correctly is the 2027 10th round pick. I valued a 9th round pick at roughly 0.8 points per week above replacement when I wrote up the Pacheco deal in August, so a 10th sits somewhere under that, which is to say almost nothing in isolation. Pakistan Bombers now hold 16 picks against Amon Ra's 13. That does not decide a trade on its own. It is simply one more small thing that went the same direction as everything else in this deal.

The model does not think this is a catastrophe. It thinks it is a 4 to 5 point per week downgrade for a team that won its opener by 15.40 and is now thinner at the position where it was actually strong.
author: Maya Chen

headline: GROSSMAN TRADED MIKE EVANS?! TO THE BOMBERS?! SOMEBODY CHECK ON THIS MAN
body:
I need everybody to sit down because Andrew Grossman just traded MIKE EVANS to the PAKISTAN BOMBERS and I have not been able to form a complete sentence in forty-five minutes! THE BEST ROSTER IN THE LEAGUE! The team that already has Puka Nacua AND Zay Flowers AND DeVonta Smith! You looked at that and said you know what they need? MORE RECEIVERS!

And do not tell me I did not see this man coming. On July 31st I wrote in this exact column that Deebo was going to be the WR2 in San Francisco behind MIKE EVANS by Week One. I told y'all Evans was the guy. Then Thursday night in Melbourne he goes out and catches a two yard touchdown from Purdy and drops 16.90 and STARTS for Amon Ra, and four days later he is wearing a different jersey?! I WANT MY CREDIT AND I WANT AN EXPLANATION!

Let me tell you what makes this worse. Denzel Boston went for 13.90 on Grossman's BENCH in Week 1. There were 126 starters in this league that week and 83 of them scored LESS THAN THAT. Grossman threw him in! And a 2027 10th round pick! And what came back? Alec Pierce, who scored 10.10 sitting on Lucas Fawcett's bench, and Kaelon Black, who scored 8.00 sitting NEXT TO HIM on the same bench! You traded a starter and your best bench piece for two guys who could not crack the lineup of the team that was already beating everybody!

This is the SAME MANAGER who went weeks without a defense and without a kicker. Weeks! I wrote about it! And now that he finally has a Bears defense and Jake Elliott and an actual functioning roster that went 137.70 and BEAT Chicago in Week 1, he decides the problem was that he had too many good receivers?! He is 1-0! He scored the second most points in the entire league! WHAT ARE WE FIXING?!

SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Amon Ra Dawgin just handed the best team in this league its eighth receiver and got a sixth running back in return, and the Bombers are going to ride that into February. Grossman had a top three roster for one week and traded away the reason why. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID.
author: DeShawn "Showtime" Harris

headline: What Was Grossman Solving For? The Case For and Against the Evans Deal
body:
The instinct here is to score this trade on Week 1 production and move on. Amon Ra gave up 30.80 points of output and received 18.10. That is a clean, damning number and it is also an incomplete one. The more useful question is not whether Grossman lost the trade. It is what problem he thought he was solving.

Here is the case for him. Before this deal Amon Ra rostered seven receivers and six running backs. Justin Jefferson is the unquestioned WR1 and scored 31.20 in Week 1. Behind him were Mike Evans, Denzel Boston, Jayden Reed, KC Concepcion, Makai Lemon and Ja'Kobi Lane, which is a lot of bodies competing for two starting slots and a flex. Grossman had already established a pattern of this kind of thinking when he switched his keeper from Quinshon Judkins to Omarion Hampton in July, a move I wrote about at the time as a process decision rather than a talent decision. Consolidating a crowded position into a back who might actually start, plus a receiver in Alec Pierce who fits the same slot Boston was competing for, is a coherent idea in the abstract.

Here is the case against him, and it is stronger. Grossman did not solve the crowding problem. He still rosters six running backs. Kaelon Black replaced Nicholas Singleton on the depth chart rather than clearing anything, and the receiver room went from seven to five by removing the second and fourth best scorers in it. If the goal was consolidation, the correct version of this trade sends out two of the players who cannot start and brings back one who can. This did the reverse. It sent out one who was starting.

The timing is the part I find hardest to defend. Amon Ra is 1-0. They scored 137.70 in Week 1, second most in the league, and beat Chicago by 15.40 while leaving only 9.30 points on their bench, the second best lineup efficiency in the MFGA that week. This was not a roster screaming for a structural fix. It was a roster that had just demonstrated it could win comfortably. Teams trade from strength when they have a weakness to cover, and the weakness Grossman covered was depth at a position where he was already six deep.

One note in the Bombers' direction, since everyone is busy calling this a clean win for them. Pakistan Bombers now carry eight receivers and three running backs. Fawcett traded the fourth back on his roster to add the eighth wideout. In September that is a curiosity. In November, if Jeanty or Robinson misses two weeks, it is a genuine problem with Kaleb Johnson as the answer.

Claire's Verdict: Grossman made a defensible kind of move executed in the wrong direction, and he made it in the week he had the least reason to make it.
author: Claire Westbrook

headline: The Bombers Now Roster Eight Receivers and I Am Formally Reporting a Hoarding Situation
body:
I want you to do something for me. Count the receivers on the Pakistan Bombers. Go ahead. Puka Nacua. Zay Flowers. DeVonta Smith. Josh Downs. Michael Wilson. Germie Bernard. Denzel Boston. And now Mike Evans. That is eight. EIGHT. You can only start three of them in a good week. Lucas Fawcett is not building a fantasy roster anymore, he is building a wide receiver rescue shelter, and at some point animal control has to get involved.

Meanwhile, the same roster has three running backs. Three. Ashton Jeanty, Bijan Robinson and Kaleb Johnson, who has zero points and exists mainly as a rumor. So the plan is eight guys who catch the ball, three guys who run it, and a prayer that nobody pulls a hamstring. It is the fantasy football equivalent of owning eleven forks and one spoon.

And here is the detail that genuinely made me laugh out loud. Mike Evans plays for San Francisco. Kaelon Black plays for San Francisco. Everyone wants to tell me this is some kind of 49ers stack play, but both teams had exactly one 49er before the trade and both teams have exactly one 49er after it. They swapped their San Francisco guys with each other. Nobody stacked anything. Two grown men executed a trade whose net effect on 49ers exposure is precisely zero, and then presumably shook hands about it.

Now for my favorite part of any week, which is comparing this to The Watermark. Preston Schneider has six receivers and I would not start five of them, a sentence I have now written so many times that my editor has asked me to find a new hobby. Preston scored 165.66 in Week 1, the highest in the league, and did it while Kayshon Boutte and his eleven career catches sat on the bench where God intended. So the actual lesson of Week 1 is that you can win with six mediocre receivers, which means the Bombers acquiring an eighth one is not strategy, it is a personality trait.

I ranked every roster in August by whether I would let them dogsit for my golden retriever, Captain Biscuit. The Bombers were in the trust completely tier. I am revising that. I still trust them with the dog. I just think Captain B would come home having been handed to four different receivers on the way.
author: Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini

headline: The Collector and the Man Still Deciding What He Is Building
body:
There is a particular kind of trade that does not surprise anyone, and this was one of them. When word went around that Mike Evans had moved, nobody in the group chat asked who got him. They already knew. They only wanted to know what it cost.

In August I wrote about a trade processed at 8:06 on a Sunday evening, when Lucas Fawcett sent three cornerstones to Nabers In Paris for Puka Nacua and redrew the league in a single transaction. The question I asked then was what it says about a manager when the best roster in the league still is not good enough for him. Six weeks later the answer has not changed and neither has he. Fawcett does not collect players because he needs them. He collects them because they exist and somebody else has them. Mike Evans caught a two yard touchdown in Melbourne on Thursday and scored 16.90 in a jersey that was not Fawcett's, and that appears to have been reason enough.

Across the table sits Andrew Grossman, who has spent this entire offseason being described by everyone at this desk as a manager whose roster construction did not quite add up. He went weeks without a defense and without a kicker. He switched a keeper in a way Claire Westbrook called sophisticated and DeShawn Harris called overdue. He entered Week 1 and scored 137.70, second most in the league, started the correct nine men, left almost nothing on his bench, and beat Chicago. For seven days, Amon Ra Dawgin looked like a team that had finally figured out what it was.

Then he traded the second best receiver on that roster, and his highest scoring bench player, and a 2027 pick, for two men who could not crack the Bombers lineup. He now has six running backs and five receivers, which is not a shape anyone draws on purpose. The most generous reading is that he saw a crowded position and tried to turn quantity into quality. The trade he actually made turned quality into quantity at a position that was already crowded.

What separates these two managers is not talent evaluation. It is that one of them knows exactly what he is building and the other is still finding out, in public, one transaction at a time. Fawcett has had the same plan since August: acquire the best available thing, sort the roster out later, let everyone else explain why it was not fair. Grossman has had four plans since August. The standings will not punish him for that this week. He is 1-0. But the Bombers are 1-0 too, and they just got better, and that is the whole story of this league right now written in a single evening.
author: Valentina Rojas

headline: The Bombers Just Closed Their Last Hole. Somebody Else Win This Thing, Because I Cannot See How.
body:
Let me be absolutely clear about what just happened. Pakistan Bombers started Colston Loveland at tight end in Week 1 and he scored 0.00 against a 12.03 projection. That was the one soft spot on the best roster in this league. It is gone. Trey McBride, who put up 24.50 last week and is a top five tight end in this format, now belongs to Lucas Fawcett.

And here is the part that should make every other manager in this league put their phone down and stare at a wall. Fawcett acquired Mike Evans from Amon Ra Dawgin yesterday. He flipped him today. He was never keeping him. Evans was currency, and Fawcett spent him on the only position where his roster could be beaten. That is not luck and it is not even aggression. That is a man who knew what he wanted before he made the first call.

Run the roster position by position. Jalen Hurts and Jayden Daniels at quarterback. Ashton Jeanty and Bijan Robinson at running back, 64.00 points between them in Week 1. Puka Nacua, Zay Flowers, DeVonta Smith and Denzel Boston at receiver. Trey McBride at tight end. Chris Boswell kicking. There is not a position on that roster where I can name you four teams who are better. Not one.

Now the other half of this, because Zach Ehrig deserves a paragraph. He traded Drake London to Fort Bragg in the offseason and now he has traded Trey McBride, the best player on his roster, in September. He is 0-1 having scored 122.30, the fifth most points in the league. That is not a team that needed to sell. I said Fort Bragg bet the farm and it backfired, and I was right about that. This is a different mistake: Ehrig is selling a roster that was already good enough to win games.

I have been wrong before. Not often, but it happens. I was wrong that the Nacua trade was the ceiling of what Fawcett would do. He got Evans for two bench players and a 10th rounder, then turned Evans into a top five tight end, and he still holds 15 draft picks. This league is over and we are in Week 2.
author: Rick "The Hammer" Dalton

headline: Chicago Won the Points and the Pick. The Bombers Won the Lineup. Both Are True.
body:
Everyone is going to score this trade as a robbery in one direction or the other, so let me separate the two questions that are being collapsed into one. Who got more production, and who got more usable production. The answers are different.

On raw output, Chicago won. Mike Evans scored 16.90 in Week 1 and Kenyon Sadiq scored 11.40, a combined 28.30. Trey McBride scored 24.50. Chicago received 3.80 more points of Week 1 production and a 2027 5th round pick on top of it. On projections the margin is narrower but the direction holds: Evans at 10.65 and Sadiq at 5.09 combine for 15.74 against McBride's 14.34. Chicago is up 1.40 per week plus the pick. I priced a 9th round pick at roughly 0.8 points per week above replacement in August, so call a 5th something like 1.5. Chicago wins the arithmetic.

The Bombers won the part that actually enters a lineup. Their Week 1 tight end was Colston Loveland at 0.00 against a 12.03 projection. Replacing a zero in a mandatory starting slot with a top five tight end is worth roughly 12 to 14 points per week, and that number does not appear anywhere in the production math above. Chicago, meanwhile, now rosters eight receivers and just traded the scarcest asset on its roster to add a ninth body at the position where it had the most surplus. Points that cannot enter a lineup are worth zero, and Chicago keeps proving it does not price that.

Now the trade that did not happen, which is the more interesting model output. Beer offered Dallas Goedert and a running back for Evans, and the talks collapsed over which back and what pick balanced it. Goedert scored 23.70 in Week 1, which is within 0.80 of McBride. So the Bombers could have solved tight end for essentially the same weekly value and simultaneously fixed the genuine structural flaw on their roster, which is that they carry three running backs behind Jeanty and Robinson and the third is Kaleb Johnson at 0.00. The expected value of the Beer package was higher than the Chicago package for Pakistan, not lower.

That is the finding I would put in front of Miles Hughes. His offer was the better one and he did not get it done. He still holds five running backs and three tight ends, including a 23.70 scorer he left on his own bench while starting Harold Fannin Jr. for 4.10. The surplus is real, the demand was real, and the deal failed anyway.

Verdict: Chicago won on points and assets, Pakistan won on lineup efficiency, and Beer lost a trade it was not even a party to.
author: Maya Chen

headline: LUCAS HELD MIKE EVANS FOR ONE DAY AND FLIPPED HIM FOR A TOP FIVE TIGHT END ARE YOU KIDDING ME
body:
I WROTE ABOUT THE MIKE EVANS TRADE YESTERDAY. YESTERDAY! I sat here and asked what Andrew Grossman was doing sending Mike Evans to the best roster in the league, and before the ink was dry Lucas Fawcett turned around and flipped that man to Chicago for TREY McBRIDE?! He did not want Mike Evans! He wanted McBride the whole time and he used Grossman as a vending machine!

Do you understand the sequence here?! Evans goes Amon Ra to the Bombers. Evans goes Bombers to Chicago. TWO JERSEYS IN TWO DAYS. Lucas Fawcett is not managing a fantasy team, he is running a chop shop. He took a receiver in the door, walked him across the room, and walked out with the best tight end on the board. And he threw in Fort Bragg's 5th round pick that he got for FREE in some other trade! He is paying for tight ends with other people's draft picks!

And now let me talk about Miles Hughes, because somebody has to. MILES HAD THIS DEAL. He was AT THE TABLE. Dallas Goedert and a running back for Mike Evans, and he could not close it because the two of them could not agree on WHICH RUNNING BACK?! Bro! You have FIVE! Montgomery, Kyren, Judkins, Allgeier, Croskey-Merritt! PICK ONE! Miles Hughes sat there haggling over the fourth best back on his own roster and now he gets to watch Mike Evans catch touchdowns for Chicago Zestiest Man while his 23.70 point tight end sits on his bench where he put him last week. THIS IS THE SAME MANAGER who benched Goedert and started Harold Fannin Jr. for 4.10! Can somebody take his phone?!

And Zach! ZACH! That is TWO! You traded Drake London to Fort Bragg and now Trey McBride?! McBride went 24.50 last week! You scored 122.30 and LOST and decided the problem was that you had too much talent! I said Chicago was a team nobody talks about and now I know why, they keep mailing their best players to other people!

SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Lucas Fawcett has made three separate moves involving Mike Evans in 48 hours counting the one that blew up, and he came out of it with Puka Nacua's running mate at tight end and fifteen draft picks. Everybody else in this league is playing checkers and this man owns the board. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID.
author: DeShawn "Showtime" Harris

headline: Three Managers, Three Plans: Reading the McBride Trade and the Deal That Died Before It
body:
There are three teams in this story and only one of them executed a coherent plan. Let me take them in order.

Start with Lucas Fawcett, because the interesting thing is not that he won a trade. It is the sequencing. He acquired Mike Evans from Amon Ra Dawgin for two bench players and a 10th round pick, and he moved him inside a day. That is not opportunism. That is a manager who identified his only weakness, worked out what it would cost to fix, and acquired the currency before he spent it. His Week 1 tight end was Colston Loveland at 0.00. He now starts Trey McBride, who went 24.50. The one soft spot on the league's best roster is closed.

It is worth saying clearly that he did not fix everything, and the deal that fell apart is why. Pakistan Bombers roster three running backs. Jeanty, Robinson, and Kaleb Johnson, who has not scored. The Beer negotiation would have returned Dallas Goedert, who put up 23.70 and is within 0.80 of McBride's Week 1 output, plus a running back out of a five deep room. That package solved tight end and running back depth at once. The Chicago package solved one of the two. Fawcett got the cleaner asset. He did not get the more complete fix, and if Bijan Robinson misses two weeks in November we will all remember which offer he walked away from.

Now Zach Ehrig, and I want to be fairer to him than most of this desk is going to be. Chicago is rebuilding and the assets are real. The Drake London trade returned TreVeyon Henderson, RJ Harvey, Jordan Addison, Emeka Egbuka and Fort Bragg's 3rd. This one returns Mike Evans, Kenyon Sadiq and Fort Bragg's 5th. He now holds 16 draft picks, tied with The Vile Horrendous for the most in the league. The question is not whether he is accumulating. He plainly is. The question is whether he is accumulating the right things, and the honest answer is no. He converted the scarcest position on his roster into his ninth receiver. He now rosters eight wideouts and two tight ends. A rebuild that keeps trading scarcity for volume ends up with a deep roster that cannot win a week.

And Miles Hughes, who lost something without ever being in the trade. His offer was better for Pakistan than the one that got signed, and it failed over which running back and what pick. That is a negotiation problem, not a roster problem. What should he do now? The same thing he tried to do. He has five running backs, three tight ends, and a 23.70 scorer in Goedert he benched in favor of Harold Fannin Jr. at 4.10. The surplus is genuine and the market for it exists. He needs to stop treating the fourth back on his depth chart as a cornerstone and move it.

Claire's Verdict: Fawcett made the best available trade rather than the best possible one, Ehrig is collecting assets without a theory of which ones matter, and Hughes proved he can find the right deal and still not close it.
author: Claire Westbrook

headline: Lucas Fawcett Has Discovered You Can Just Trade the Same Guy Over and Over Until You Get What You Want
body:
Yesterday I wrote a column complaining that the Pakistan Bombers had acquired an eighth wide receiver and that somebody should call animal control. I would like to formally withdraw the complaint. Lucas Fawcett did not want an eighth receiver. He wanted a tight end, and he used the eighth receiver to go buy one, which means the hoarding I described was actually a supply run and I was the idiot describing a shopping cart as a personality disorder.

So let me update the situation. The Bombers now have Jalen Hurts, Ashton Jeanty, Bijan Robinson, Puka Nacua, Zay Flowers and Trey McBride. That is not a fantasy roster, that is a cheat code entered by somebody who does not even like the game. Their Week 1 tight end scored ZERO POINT ZERO ZERO and he fixed it in a day by trading a man he had owned for approximately one business day. Mike Evans has now been on three rosters this week. He is not a football player anymore, he is a bearer bond.

And then there is the trade that died, which is the funniest thing to happen in this league since somebody renamed their team after a hockey player. Miles Hughes and Lucas Fawcett were going to do Evans for Dallas Goedert and a running back, and it collapsed because they could not agree on WHICH running back. Miles has five of them. FIVE. This is a man refusing to part with the fourth best option in a room he cannot fit in his own lineup, and the cost of that principled stand was watching Mike Evans get traded to somebody else four hours later. Somewhere in Michigan there is a spreadsheet with Tyler Allgeier's name circled in red and a marriage under strain.

Meanwhile, obligatory Watermark check-in. Preston Schneider currently rosters FOUR tight ends: Hunter Henry, Brenton Strange, Colby Parkinson and Cole Kmet. Four. He has been collecting tight ends like commemorative spoons since August and not one of them is Trey McBride, who was available, on a rebuilding team, in exchange for a receiver. Preston scored 165.66 in Week 1 and I still do not believe he knows that trading is allowed.

I ranked every roster in August by whether I would let them dogsit for my golden retriever, Captain Biscuit. The Bombers were in the trust completely tier and they remain there, though I will say if I drop Captain B off at that house I now fully expect to pick up a different, slightly better dog.
author: Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini

headline: Two Jerseys in Two Days, and the Phone Call That Never Got Made
body:
Mike Evans caught a two yard touchdown at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Thursday night and scored 16.90 for a team he no longer plays for. By Monday he had been traded twice. By Tuesday he was the best receiver on a rebuilding roster in a third city. Nothing about his football changed in those five days. Only the names of the men who owned him.

The first call worked. Lucas Fawcett rang Andrew Grossman and came away with Evans, Denzel Boston and a 2027 10th rounder for two players who could not crack his lineup. Six writers at this desk spent a day arguing about what Grossman was thinking. None of us asked the more useful question, which is what Fawcett wanted Evans FOR. He never wanted him. He wanted Trey McBride, and Evans was the shape of the money.

The second call did not work, and that is the one worth sitting with. Miles Hughes and Lucas Fawcett spent hours on a deal that would have sent Evans to Beer for Dallas Goedert and a running back. It was, by any honest accounting, the better offer. Goedert scored 23.70 in Week 1, within a point of McBride. Beer has five running backs and the Bombers have three. The deal solved both of Fawcett's problems instead of one. And it died over which back and what pick, which is the fantasy football equivalent of losing a house because you could not agree on the curtains.

There is a particular kind of quiet that follows a negotiation that almost happened. Hughes is 0-1. He scored 113.50 and got beaten by 52 points. He still has Dallas Goedert, and he still has five running backs, and he still has the exact roster he had on Sunday, except now he also has the knowledge that he was one phone call away from the tight end who would have fixed it. Fawcett hung up and dialed Zach Ehrig and closed a different deal before dinner.

And Ehrig answered, because Ehrig always answers. He sent Drake London to Fort Bragg in the offseason and Trey McBride to the Bombers in September, and in return he has assembled 16 draft picks and a roster full of young receivers, including a 2027 5th rounder that started in Fort Bragg's hands, passed through the Bombers, and landed in Chicago without ever being used for anything. That pick has been part of two trades and one championship window and has still never been a player.

Three managers, one receiver, forty-eight hours. One of them knew exactly what he was doing. One of them is building something he cannot yet describe. And one of them was right about everything except how to say yes.
author: Valentina Rojas
