headline: GAME DAY BURN: New House, Old Gods, and the 0-2 Harrison Bragg Has Never Seen
body:
Vibe check: they built a brand new football stadium in Buffalo, opened the doors for the first time, and the very first thing that ever happened inside it was Josh Allen scoring five touchdowns and hanging 40.82 on a fantasy scoreboard. 60,644 people walked into the new Highmark Stadium for the first regular season game ever played there. The Bills scored on their first three possessions. 21-0 before Detroit did anything worth writing down. That is not a home opener, that is a housewarming where the host drinks all the wine, eats all the food, and hands the guests the bill on the way out.

Bills 41, Lions 31. ZERO turnovers in the entire game by either team, which basically never happens. Buffalo went 9 for 12 on third down, 5 for 5 in the red zone, ran for 203 yards, and held the ball for 33:45. Detroit hung 31 on the board and it was never close for one second.

I pulled the ESPN box score AND all fourteen Week 2 lineups, because half the fun is who left points rotting on the bench and the other half, as always, is Harrison Bragg.

JOSH ALLEN: 20/31, 248 yards, 3 TD, plus 14 carries for 69 yards and 2 more TD. 40.82. Started at QB by Pluto Shraazinatorz (Shreyus).

FIVE touchdowns. Projected 22.69, delivered 40.82, an 18.13-point overage and the highest single-game score anybody in this league has posted all season, past Caleb Williams's 37.26 from Week 1. The three passing scores went to three different guys - Joshua Palmer 43 yards on 3rd and 11, Dawson Knox from the 1, Dalton Kincaid from 16 - and then Allen just ran in the other two himself from the 1 and the 2. If you cannot throw it in, walk it in. Revolutionary.

Shreyus now has 76.48 points out of one quarterback in two weeks. That is more than Fort Bragg's entire starting lineup scored in Week 1. We will come back to that.

AMON-RA ST. BROWN: 9 catches, 142 yards, 2 TD on THIRTEEN targets. 35.20. Started at WR by Pavel Dorofeyev (Miles).

Thirteen targets in a game his team trailed by three scores. Projected 20.37, delivered 35.20. A 34-yard bomb, a 2-yard touchdown, and a 27-yard touchdown with 1:42 left that nobody in Buffalo cared about and Miles cared about enormously.

And here is the genuinely beautiful part: Miles started Amon-Ra St. Brown AND the Lions D/ST in the same football game. He got 35.20 from one and handed 4.00 of it straight back, because his own defense had to stand there and get shelled by Josh Allen. Net 31.20. He bet on the game and against the game simultaneously and the game charged him a service fee.

JARED GOFF: 26/38, 327 yards, 4 TD, ZERO interceptions, sacked 4 times. 29.78. Started at QB by Doob's Agency (Matt).

Projected 17.02. Delivered 29.78. Four touchdowns and a clean sheet in a ten-point loss, which is the most Jared Goff sentence ever written. And look who it is. Matt Gingrich, last week's DICK OF THE DAY, the man who benched an 18-point Deebo Samuel game and got roasted in this column for it, just started the right quarterback and cleared his projection by 12.76. Growth. I am proud of him. It will not last.

JAHMYR GIBBS: 16 carries, 52 yards, plus 6 catches for 61 and a TD on 8 targets. 23.30. Started at RB by The Watermark (Preston).

3.3 a carry on the ground, because Detroit ran for 66 yards as a team and Buffalo's front spent the night living in their backfield. Did not matter. Eight targets, an 11-yard touchdown catch, and PPR paid him like he had a great night.

DALTON KINCAID: 7 catches, 95 yards, 1 TD on 8 targets. 22.50. Started at TE by Amon Ra Dawgin (Andrew).

Projected 10.42 and more than DOUBLED it. A 25-yard dig in the first, a 23-yarder down to the Detroit 6 in the third, and the 16-yard touchdown that made it 27-7. Andrew Grossman spent this entire week getting dragged across every column on this news desk for trading Mike Evans away, and then his tight end quietly put 22.50 on the board on a Thursday. Nobody else is going to mention it. I am mentioning it.

Small note: Tyler Bass MISSED the extra point after Kincaid's touchdown, went 5 for 6 on the night, and did not attempt a single field goal. A kicker with zero field goal attempts in a 41-point game is a bouncer at a party nobody tried to sneak into.

JAMES COOK III: 21 carries, 135 yards, 1 TD, plus a catch for 4. 20.90. Started at RB by The Vile Horrendous (Evan).

6.4 a carry. A 35-yard run behind left guard, a 22-yarder down to the Detroit 1 in the fourth, and then the 1-yard punch-in that made it 41-24 and ended the argument. Beat his 18.65 projection.

And here is the matchup inside the matchup: Preston and Evan are playing each other this week and their two guys were on the same field. Gibbs 23.30, Cook 20.90. Preston leads by 2.40 on the strength of six receptions. Two men watched the exact same game and felt the opposite thing every twelve seconds.

SAM LAPORTA: 6 catches, 52 yards, 1 TD on 7 targets. 17.20. Started at TE by I Heart Gingers (Carter).

Projected 11.24. The big one was an 18-yard grab on 4TH AND 5 at the Buffalo 40 in the third, on a drive that ended in a Detroit touchdown. Then he caught the 1-yard score himself in the fourth. Carter is 0-1 and needed exactly this.

JAKE BATES: 1 for 1 from 31 yards, 4 for 4 on extra points. 7.00. Started at K by Starving Ethiopians (Stephen).

His field goal came as the first half clock hit 0:00, after Detroit went 65 yards in 39 seconds to set it up. Efficient, forgettable, and the second-highest total on Stephen's night, which tells you everything about how Stephen's night went.

KHALIL SHAKIR: 3 catches, 38 yards on 6 targets. 6.80. BENCHED by Miles.

He also recovered Detroit's onside kick with 1:42 to go, which pays nothing and looked cool.

JAMESON WILLIAMS: 2 catches, 33 yards on 4 targets. 5.30. Started at WR by Stephen.

Projected 12.32, in a game where his quarterback threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns, and he walked out with two catches. Four targets on a 38-attempt night. Goff looked at him the way you look at a coworker whose name you forgot.

ISAAC TESLAA: 2 catches, 26 yards on 5 targets. 4.60. Benched by Stephen. One more target than Jameson Williams got, and a 20-yard grab on 4TH AND 18. Stephen picked wrong by 0.70, the least consequential bench crime in recorded history.

SIONE VAKI: 1 carry for 7, 1 catch for 13. 3.00. Benched by Shreyus, who was otherwise busy owning Josh Allen.

RAY DAVIS: ZERO carries, zero targets, one 31-yard kickoff return. 0.00. Benched by Evan, correctly.

TY JOHNSON: OUT with a hamstring, did not dress. 0.00. Benched by Matt, also correctly.

ISIAH PACHECO: on Stephen's IR, watched the whole thing from Detroit in street clothes.

LIONS D/ST: 41 points allowed, 2 sacks, zero interceptions, zero fumble recoveries, zero takeaways of any kind. MINUS FOUR POINTS. Started by Miles.

Aidan Hutchinson and Derrick Barnes got the sacks and that is the entire highlight package. When your defense's contribution to the box score is a negative number, that is not a unit, that is a donation.

DJ MOORE: 1 carry for MINUS ONE YARD. Zero catches. Injured. MINUS 0.10. STARTED at WR by Fort Bragg (Harrison).

Let that sit for a second. Then keep reading, because it gets so much worse.

STUD OF THE NIGHT: Josh Allen, 40.82, five touchdowns, 18.13 over projection, in the first game ever played inside his team's new building. Shreyus Saxena did nothing on Thursday except own the correct quarterback, and it has him up 18.32 on Andrew with three days still to play. Some weeks the roster works while you sleep.

DICK OF THE DAY: DJ MOORE, and by extension the man who started him.

Here is the complete DJ Moore game log from Thursday night. One carry, an end around at 4:33 of the first quarter, for MINUS ONE YARD. One target, a Josh Allen incompletion in the red zone at 3:01 of the second, on which DJ Moore was INJURED and which was then WIPED OFF THE BOARD ENTIRELY by a Dawson Knox holding penalty. That is it. That is the whole night. A play that lost a yard and a play that did not legally happen. Final line: minus 0.10 points against a 12.54 projection, and a shoulder.

Now the part that should make Harrison Bragg sit down. LAST WEEK, DJ Moore went for over 100 yards on eight targets and scored 21.00 points. HARRISON HAD HIM ON THE BENCH. This week he promoted him into the starting lineup and Moore returned a NEGATIVE NUMBER. Twenty-one on the bench, minus a tenth in the lineup. The man is running a perfect inverse of his own roster, like a guy who sells the stock the day before it doubles and buys it back the day before it craters.

And that 21.00 he benched last week would not even have saved him, because Fort Bragg lost Week 1 by 32.78. That is the only mercy in this paragraph and it is not much of one.

BENCH CRIMES: Thin ledger tonight, because one game has been played and most of the damage is still loaded in the chamber for Sunday.

Miles benched Khalil Shakir (6.80) while starting a Lions defense that scored MINUS 4.00. Different roster slots, so he could not have swapped them straight across, but there is something poetic about a manager holding a live Bills receiver in reserve while trotting out the unit whose entire job was to stop the Bills.

Stephen started Jameson Williams (5.30) over Isaac TeSlaa (4.60), a 0.70 miss, and got 12.30 total out of FOUR rostered Lions in a game where Detroit scored 31 points and threw for 327 yards. That is not a lineup error, that is a diversification error. He owns a kicker, a WR3, a bench receiver and an IR running back from the same offense. The offense went off. He got twelve points. It is like holding four different index funds that all secretly own the same one stock, except the stock went UP and you somehow still lost money.

And the real crime of the night is not a bench at all. It is Harrison Bragg promoting a 21-point bench receiver into his starting lineup exactly one week too late and getting minus 0.10 for it. See above. See this whole column, honestly.

INJURY REPORT: DJ MOORE took a shoulder on that erased red zone incompletion at 3:01 of the second quarter and is QUESTIONABLE. Fort Bragg's starting receiver, his only player in the game, already worth negative points, and now hurt. When you are already in a hole, the shovel breaking is not good news.

TY JOHNSON (hamstring) was OUT for Buffalo, which Matt Gingrich correctly saw coming. T.J. SANDERS (knee) and ED OLIVER (hip) were both OUT for the Bills and Buffalo's front still put up 4 sacks and 10 quarterback hits, with Greg Rousseau alone accounting for 2 sacks and 4 hits. AVONTE MADDOX is QUESTIONABLE with a foot for Detroit. None of those men are on a roster in this league, so nobody here has to perform grief.

And the injury that actually matters this week happened in a different stadium entirely. KYLER MURRAY took a hard shot to the head in Week 1, is under concussion evaluation, and is very likely out for an extended stretch. Carson Wentz has Minnesota's job now. Fort Bragg's Week 1 starting quarterback, the man who posted MINUS 0.38 in a 65.52-point loss, is now benched AND concussed, and Harrison is starting Patrick Mahomes on Sunday. Which is exactly what he should have done in Week 1, when Mahomes put up 21.66 in a polo shirt while Kyler was busy going negative. Also on Fort Bragg's IR: JOSH JACOBS, day to day.

SCOREBOARD CHECK, Week 2, started players only, through Thursday night:

Pluto Shraazinatorz 40.82, Amon Ra Dawgin 22.50. Shreyus got every point of it from one man. Andrew got a career night out of Dalton Kincaid and is still down 18.32. Both teams are 1-0 and this is the best matchup on the board.

Pavel Dorofeyev 31.20, Mount Olympus 0. Miles took 35.20 from St. Brown, gave 4.00 of it back to his own defense, and still walked out of Thursday with the second-biggest lead in the league. Liam had nobody in this game.

Doob's Agency 29.78, Chicago Zestiest Man 0. Matt's entire night was Jared Goff and it was enough to build a 29.78 cushion on a Zach Ehrig roster that has not scored a point yet.

The Watermark 23.30, The Vile Horrendous 20.90. Gibbs and Cook, same field, 2.40 apart, and both managers still have full Sunday rosters coming. Closest live matchup in the league.

I Heart Gingers 17.20, Englewood Ninjas 0. Carter got LaPorta. Drew, who dropped 98.30 on Fort Bragg in Week 1, had nobody in this game and has to sit on a goose egg until Sunday.

Starving Ethiopians 12.30, Fort Bragg MINUS 0.10. Read that line again. The defending champion of this league is LOSING TO A NEGATIVE NUMBER and the negative number is his own.

Pakistan Bombers 0, VancouverPantiesDeJarome 0. Neither team had a single player in the game. Lucas and Josh P start Sunday from zero like civilized people.

LOOKING AHEAD: HARRISON BRAGG HAS NEVER BEEN 0-2

I went through every season this franchise has ever played. All of it. Here is what came back, and I want everybody to understand how strange this is.

2022: Fort Bragg won Week 1, lost Week 2. 1-1. Finished 12-1 and WON THE CHAMPIONSHIP.
2023: Lost Week 1, won Week 2. 1-1. Finished 6-7.
2024: Won Week 1, lost Week 2. 1-1. Finished 4-9.
2025: Lost Week 1, won Week 2. 1-1. Finished 9-4 and WON THE CHAMPIONSHIP AGAIN.

Four seasons in this league. Four times 1-1 after two weeks. Every single year, no exceptions, no deviation. HARRISON BRAGG HAS NEVER BEEN 0-2 IN THE HISTORY OF THIS LEAGUE. He has never lost two games in a row to open a season, not once, and both years he dropped his opener, 2023 and 2025, he turned around and won Week 2 immediately. One of those years ended with a trophy in his hands.

He is staring down the barrel of it this weekend.

Fort Bragg is 0-1. Week 1 he scored 65.52, the LOWEST TOTAL IN THE ENTIRE LEAGUE, and lost to Englewood by 32.78 while Patrick Mahomes (21.66) and DJ Moore (21.00) sat on his bench and his starting quarterback scored MINUS 0.38. Every reporter on this site called him the clown of the week. He has already lost his only Thursday player to a shoulder and he is currently trailing a negative number.

Sunday he plays the STARVING ETHIOPIANS, who are 0-1, who have never made the playoffs in franchise history, who are 9-30 all time, and who own the worst winning percentage of any active team in this league. Loser of this game goes 0-2. One of these two men is about to have something happen to him that has never happened before.

The good news for Harrison: he finally benched Kyler Murray, he is starting Mahomes, and projections have Fort Bragg at 109.2 against Stephen's 105.0, the second-closest projected matchup of the week. The bad news: he is down 12.40 before Sunday even starts, his only player so far actively cost him points, Josh Jacobs is on IR, and the man across from him owns four Detroit Lions who just handed him twelve points out of a 31-point game, which means there is an enormous amount of room for Stephen to simply be less bad than he was on Thursday.

Two-time champion, defending title holder, staring at the first 0-2 of his life, against a franchise that has never won anything. If that is not the game of the week I do not know what is.

THE REST OF SUNDAY

Pakistan Bombers at VancouverPantiesDeJarome is the projection mismatch of the week, 138.8 to 118.4, and it is the TREY McBRIDE DEBUT. Lucas Fawcett took Mike Evans off Andrew on Monday, held him for roughly one day, then flipped him to Zach for a top-five tight end. McBride opens Week 2 in the Bombers' starting lineup against Seattle, coming off a 9-catch, 13-target, 95-yard, 1-touchdown Week 1. Josh P is 0-1 with 76.86 points and three running backs on his entire roster. Zay Flowers being QUESTIONABLE in Lucas's FLEX is the only crack in that wall.

The other half of that trade is live too. MIKE EVANS starts at WR for Chicago Zestiest Man against Tennessee, and Zach is already down 29.78 to Matt Gingrich. Zach won the points and the pick in that deal and now has to actually go score with them, from a roster carrying Tank Dell and Jordyn Tyson on IR, Jordan Mason on IR, and Jakobi Meyers and RJ Harvey both QUESTIONABLE. That is a lot of duct tape holding up one Mike Evans.

Mount Olympus at Pavel Dorofeyev is Liam chasing 31.20 with Sam Darnold OUT, Jayden Higgins on IR, and both Brian Thomas Jr. and Kyle Monangai QUESTIONABLE. Miles has Ladd McConkey QUESTIONABLE. Somebody in this matchup is going to win it with a guy they were not sure would suit up.

Englewood Ninjas at I Heart Gingers is the 1-0 team chasing the 0-1 team, because Drew had nobody Thursday and Carter had LaPorta. Drew's two Questionables are Brock Bowers and Eddy Pineiro, a tight end and a kicker, which is a strange pair of things to lie awake about.

The Watermark at The Vile Horrendous is 2.40 apart and has the tightest projected margin on the whole board, 116.9 to 119.9. Preston has Chris Olave and D'Andre Swift both QUESTIONABLE, which is his WR and his FLEX. Evan is completely healthy. Somebody is losing this by less than three points.

And Pluto at Amon Ra Dawgin is two 1-0 teams with the league's highest scorer sitting on one side of it. Shreyus has Nico Collins QUESTIONABLE. Andrew has Alec Pierce QUESTIONABLE and just traded away a receiver who put up 16.90 in his last game. He is going to spend Sunday finding out whether Kincaid's 22.50 was the win or the consolation prize.

Set your damn lineups. And Harrison, look at the bench one more time before you submit. History is sitting right there and it has never gone the other way.

headline: Five Weeks, One Game: The Whole Desk on Harrison Bragg Selling Drake London
body:
Harrison Bragg traded Drake London to the Pluto Shraazinatorz on Friday for Carnell Tate and two 2027 draft picks, a 6th and an 11th. London played one game for Fort Bragg. All six of us had something to say about it, so we are all saying it here.

RICK "THE HAMMER" DALTON: I Told You He Burned the Boats. He Just Swam Back and Asked for a Refund.

On August 13th I wrote that Fort Bragg had bet the farm on 2026 and there was no going back. I laid out the receipts. Four 2027 picks gone. Seven players shipped out. Drake London brought in as the centerpiece, and I used that word deliberately, because that is what Harrison Bragg told this league he was building around.

Here is what London cost. TreVeyon Henderson, RJ Harvey, Jordan Addison, Emeka Egbuka, and Fort Bragg's 2027 3rd round pick, all to Chicago Zestiest Man. Four players and a third rounder for one wide receiver.

Here is what London produced in a Fort Bragg uniform. One start. Week 1. 5.50 points against a 13.82 projection. That is the complete body of work. He never took a snap for this team in Week 2 because he was traded before Atlanta kicked off.

And here is what London brought back. Carnell Tate, a 6th round pick, and an 11th round pick.

So the ledger reads: four players and a 3rd in, one WR3 and two late picks out, 5.50 points of production in between. Bragg turned a 3rd round pick into a 6th and an 11th and called it a Friday. I said he had to conquer or drown. He has decided to do neither. He is treading water and selling the lifeboat for parts.

One more thing, because the detail is too good to leave out. Fort Bragg's own 6th and 11th rounders were already traded away to The Vile Horrendous. Bragg just spent his centerpiece receiver buying back the two rounds he had already sold. That is not a rebuild and it is not a push. That is a man rearranging the same furniture in a smaller apartment.

MAYA CHEN: The Production Math Says This Is Close. The Roster Math Says Shreyus Won.

Let me separate what everyone is about to collapse into one number.

On Week 1 production, Fort Bragg won this trade. Carnell Tate scored 7.80 in Pluto's FLEX. Drake London scored 5.50 in Fort Bragg's starting lineup. Bragg gave up the lower scorer and received the higher one, plus two picks. That is a 2.30 point gain and two assets. On the raw arithmetic it is not close, and nobody is going to say it out loud because of who is involved.

On projections the direction reverses. London projects 13.92 for Week 2, Tate projects 11.40. That is a 2.52 per week edge to London, which across twelve remaining regular season games is roughly 30 points. I price a 6th round pick at about 1.1 points per week above replacement and an 11th at about 0.4, so the two picks are worth something in the neighborhood of 1.5 per week starting in 2027. They are worth zero this season, and Fort Bragg is 0-1 with the lowest point total in the league.

Now the part that decides it. Shreyus Saxena entered Friday with three healthy wide receivers: George Pickens, Xavier Hutchinson, and Carnell Tate. Nico Collins, his leading receiver at 21.20, is on injured reserve. He was starting two receivers out of a room of three, with no margin for a second injury. He traded from a position of genuine scarcity into a genuine need and he paid in picks rather than in bodies, which is the correct currency when your problem is a lineup slot and not a roster spot.

Fort Bragg had six receivers before this trade and has six after. The names changed. The structural picture did not. Bragg exchanged his highest-ceiling receiver for a lower-ceiling one at the same position, in a season where he cannot afford ceiling reduction, and banked two picks for a draft he has already mortgaged four times over.

Maya's Model says: Pluto improves its weekly projection by 2.52 and closes a real hole. Fort Bragg improves its Week 1 rear-view mirror by 2.30 and acquires two picks that cannot help it win a game before February. Shreyus won.

DESHAWN "SHOWTIME" HARRIS: HE HAD HIM FOR ONE GAME! ONE!

ONE GAME! Drake London played ONE GAME for Fort Bragg! ONE! Harrison Bragg spent FOUR PLAYERS and a THIRD ROUND PICK on this man in August and got him on the field exactly ONE TIME for FIVE POINT FIVE POINTS and then MAILED HIM TO PLUTO FOR A GUY NAMED CARNELL AND TWO PICKS THAT DO NOT EXIST YET!

Do you understand what I am looking at?! Henderson! Harvey! Addison! Egbuka! A THIRD ROUNDER! All of that went to Chicago! For London! And London gave him 5.50 and a coat check ticket!

And now he sells him! For a SIXTH and an ELEVENTH! Bro, you paid a THIRD and got back a SIXTH and an ELEVENTH! That is not a trade that is a GARAGE SALE! You bought a boat, took it out once, it leaked, and you sold it for two fishing poles!

AND SHREYUS! Shreyus Saxena is 1-0, he has Josh Allen who just went 40.82 on Thursday night, he is UP 18.32 in his matchup RIGHT NOW, his best receiver got hurt and he just went out and bought a WR1 with two picks he was never going to use! THAT MAN IS PLAYING CHESS! He gave up a bench guy and pocket change!

And Harrison is sitting there at 0-1 with the LOWEST SCORE IN THE LEAGUE about to be 0-2 FOR THE FIRST TIME IN HIS LIFE and his answer is to trade his best receiver for draft picks in a draft he already SOLD FOUR ROUNDS OF! WHO IS ADVISING THIS MAN!

SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Drake London spent five weeks on Fort Bragg, played one game, scored 5.50, and left. He was a houseguest. Harrison paid four players and a 3rd round pick for a HOUSEGUEST. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID.

CLAIRE WESTBROOK: What Was He Solving For? Two Readings, and Only One of Them Works.

There are two honest ways to read this trade and I want to give both a fair hearing before I pick.

The first reading is that Harrison Bragg is cutting a loss. He paid a premium for Drake London in August, London underperformed his projection by 8.32 in the only game he played, and rather than ride a disappointing asset Bragg converted him into a comparable producer plus two picks. Carnell Tate scored more in Week 1 than London did. On that reading this is a manager correcting a mistake quickly instead of defending it out of pride, which is a real skill and one most people in this league do not have.

The second reading is that this contradicts everything Fort Bragg has done for two months. You do not trade four players and a 3rd round pick for a centerpiece receiver in August and then sell him in September for late picks unless something has changed. And the thing that changed is the record. Fort Bragg is 0-1, scored 65.52, and is a loss away from the first 0-2 start in franchise history. That is one game of evidence. One.

I pick the second reading, and here is why. Look at what Bragg actually received. If this were a rebuild, the return would be aimed at 2027 and he would be selling Mark Andrews and Davante Adams and Travis Etienne too. He is not. If this were a win-now move, the return would be a player who improves Sunday's lineup, and Tate projects 2.52 below the man he replaced. The return fits neither theory. It is a transaction made by someone reacting to a bad week rather than executing a plan, and the tell is that the assets coming back do not serve either direction.

There is also a timing problem nobody has raised. DJ Moore is questionable with a shoulder he injured on Thursday night. Bragg's receiver room going into Sunday is Tate, Davante Adams coming off 5.60, Tre Tucker, Jahan Dotson, and Malachi Fields. He traded a starting receiver two days before a game he has to win, while his other starting receiver is on the injury report.

Claire's Verdict: Saxena solved a specific problem with the correct currency. Bragg solved a feeling. The first one wins games.

TOMMY "T-BONE" MANCINI: The Man Returned a Wide Receiver Inside the Thirty Day Window

I want to be clear that I am not mad. I am delighted. This is the funniest transaction of the season and I include the one where a guy renamed his team after a hockey player.

Harrison Bragg acquired Drake London in August with the energy of a man buying a boat. He told everybody. He gave up four players and a third round pick. The receiver room was going to be London and Evans and Moore and this desk wrote roughly nine thousand words about how nobody would sleep. I personally described it as a problem for the rest of the league.

Drake London then played one football game for Fort Bragg Confederates, caught enough passes to produce 5.50 fantasy points, and was returned to the store. FIVE WEEKS. He was on that roster for five weeks and one of them was a bye for everyone because the season had not started. The man had a longer relationship with Fort Bragg's practice squad than with its starting lineup.

And the return! A sixth and an eleventh! Harrison, my guy, you paid a THIRD for him. You have now turned a 3rd round pick into a 6th and an 11th, which in the pick-value literature is what we call losing. You did the fantasy football equivalent of trading a car for a bicycle and two coupons for a different bicycle.

Also I have to note that Fort Bragg had already sold its own 6th and 11th to The Vile Horrendous. So Bragg has spent the last two months selling picks in rounds 6 and 11 and has now spent his best receiver buying picks in rounds 6 and 11. He is running a pick laundering operation and the only thing getting cleaned out is his roster.

Obligatory Watermark check-in: Preston Schneider still rosters four tight ends and has still never made a trade. He scored 165.66 in Week 1 and leads his matchup right now. At this point I believe the man is winning specifically to spite me.

I ranked every roster in August by whether I would let them dogsit for my golden retriever, Captain Biscuit. Fort Bragg was in the would trust with the dog but not the house tier. I am revising. I would not let Harrison Bragg hold my dog's leash for five weeks, because apparently that is exactly how long he keeps things.

VALENTINA ROJAS: Five Weeks, One Game, and a Receiver Who Never Belonged to Anyone

Drake London caught passes for the Atlanta Falcons on the second Sunday of September and scored 5.50 points for a man who had spent four players and a third round pick to watch him do it. Twelve days later he belonged to somebody else. Nothing about his football changed. Only the names of the men who owned him, and the story each of them was telling himself when they signed.

Harrison Bragg bought Drake London in August because he had just won a championship and decided that was not enough. That is not a criticism. It is the most human thing a defending champion can do. You hold the trophy, you look at the roster that got it for you, and all you can see is where it nearly broke. So you spend. Henderson, Harvey, Addison, Egbuka, a 3rd round pick. You give up four young men and a piece of a future draft for one receiver who is supposed to be the answer, and for about five weeks you get to believe you have solved something.

Then you score 65.52 in Week 1, the lowest total in the league, and your quarterback posts a negative number, and every writer at this desk calls you the clown of the week. And the receiver you bet the farm on gives you 5.50.

I do not think this trade is about Drake London. I think it is about what a bad Sunday does to a man's conviction. Bragg did not stop believing in London after one game. He stopped believing in the version of himself that made the August trade, and London was the most expensive piece of evidence lying around.

On the other end of the phone was Shreyus Saxena, who had a much simpler week. He owns Josh Allen, who scored 40.82 in a new stadium on Thursday night. He is 1-0 and leading. And his best receiver, Nico Collins, is on injured reserve, which left him with three healthy wideouts and a Sunday he could not cover. He needed a receiver and he had picks he was never going to spend. There was no crisis of identity in it. He just made the call.

That is the whole difference between these two men this week. One of them traded because he knew exactly what was missing. The other traded because he could not stand to look at what he had.

Drake London will play on Sunday, in the same jersey, for the same team in Atlanta, and he will score whatever he scores. The third round pick that bought him is in Chicago now, still unused, waiting on a draft that is sixteen months away. Four players are scattered across two rosters. And the man who paid for all of it has a 6th, an 11th, and a game he has to win to avoid something that has never happened to him.

He will find out on Sunday whether any of it mattered.

headline: MATCHUP BURN: Doob's Drops 167, Chicago Gets Evicted, and Bryce Young Watches Again
body:
Vibe check: Matt Gingrich hung 167.68 and beat Zach by 89.18, which is not a fantasy score, that is a hostage situation. Liam survived Miles by 5.48 in the only game worth watching. Stephen scored 62.22, the lowest number this league has produced all season.

This league left 261.42 points on the bench, down from 350.70 in Week 1, which is growth the same way falling down eleven stairs instead of fourteen is growth. Three of the seven losers lost by less than they left in the closet.

THE LOSERS

ZACH EHRIG, Chicago Zestiest Man. 78.50. Lost to Matt 167.68. Margin 89.18.

Eighty-nine points. That is not a loss, that is an eviction notice.

JAXSON DART: 0.80. Projected 18.18. Started. His quarterback produced less than one point in a PPR league, so Zach would have been better off leaving the slot empty and letting the void take snaps.

The rest is a bread line. EMEKA EGBUKA 10.30, MIKE EVANS 8.40, BUCCANEERS D/ST 4.00, KENYON SADIQ 3.70. If that roster was a restaurant the health inspector would chain the doors and burn the building for insurance.

Here is the cruel part. Zach left only 7.00 on his bench and ran 91.8% efficiency. There was nothing to fix. He played his best available lineup and lost by 89. That is not a lineup problem, that is a roster problem.

STEPHEN CERQUONE, Starving Ethiopians. 62.22. Lost to Harrison 83.68. Margin 21.46.

Lowest score in the league for the second week running.

BRYCE YOUNG: 24.08. ON THE BENCH. AGAIN.

Young went 31.44 in a polo shirt in Week 1, so Stephen responded by starting DRAKE MAYE (8.02, projected 18.23) and benching Young a second time. That is 55.52 points of quarterback watched from his own couch across two weeks. At some point this stops being a mistake and becomes a lifestyle.

MIKE GESICKI: 0.00 in the flex. TUCKER KRAFT: 3.50. RACHAAD WHITE went 14.30 on the bench. He left 32.46 behind and lost by 21.46. Optimal 94.68 and he wins going away.

EVAN BROCKWAY, The Vile Horrendous. 81.68. Lost to Preston 114.52. Margin 32.84.

Evan left 41.40 on his bench, most in the league, for the second consecutive week. This man is building a shrine.

TRAVIS KELCE: 25.10. BENCHED. Last week he benched JALEN COKER (33.80) and ISAIAH LIKELY (27.80) and started Kelce for 10.10. So this week he corrected course by starting Likely (8.30) and benching Kelce. Lineup roulette with a fully loaded chamber.

MALIK NABERS: 1.10 on a 14.93 projection. JUSTIN HERBERT: 7.88 on 19.48. Quarterback and WR1 combined for 8.98. Optimal 123.08, actual 81.68, 66.4% efficiency. He wins by nine if he can operate a dropdown menu.

CARTER COLE, I Heart Gingers. 106.40. Lost to Drew 156.48. Margin 50.08.

Ja'Marr Chase remembered he was Ja'Marr Chase (26.50 after 3.20) and it bought Carter nothing.

RHAMONDRE STEVENSON: 3.60. J.K. DOBBINS in the flex: 3.60. Two running back slots, 7.20 combined. That backfield showed up to a bar fight with a pool noodle.

BENCH CRIME, part two of a continuing series: STEFON DIGGS 21.70 and GEORGE KITTLE 18.00 both sat. I wrote about Diggs being benched last week. Carter read it, nodded, and did it again. Maya Chen had this roster Tier 1 at 9.8 projected wins. They are 0-2.

ANDREW GROSSMAN, Amon Ra Dawgin. 82.16. Lost to Shreyus 125.92. Margin 43.76.

Last week Andrew was "no notes." This week his entire roster ate at the same gas station.

JUSTIN JEFFERSON: 8.50 on 18.36. TREVOR LAWRENCE: 6.16 on 15.91. JAVONTE WILLIAMS: 8.00 on 16.70. JAYDEN REED in the flex: 1.40. ALEC PIERCE: 2.10. Five starters, 26.16 points, every one under projection.

Only 7.80 on the bench. There was no crime here. Andrew played the right nine guys and they all died together, which is somehow worse.

LUCAS FAWCETT, Pakistan Bombers. 102.46. Lost to Josh P 130.90. Margin 28.44.

Rick "The Hammer" Dalton spent August calling this the best backfield this league has ever seen. Week 1 it went 64.00. Week 2 it went 21.40.

BIJAN ROBINSON: 11.10 on 22.93. ASHTON JEANTY: 10.30 on 18.33. COLSTON LOVELAND in the flex: 1.30, one week after going 0.00. Lucas looked at a zero and said run it back.

BENCH CRIME: DENZEL BOSTON 20.50 and JOSH DOWNS 14.20 in street clothes. He left 34.60 behind and lost by 28.44. Worst efficiency in the league at 74.8%.

MILES HUGHES, Pavel Dorofeyev. 107.98. Lost to Liam 113.46. Margin 5.48.

The most brutal loss on the board. MATTHEW STAFFORD: 26.98, after I put his 4.10 in print twice. AMON-RA ST. BROWN: 35.20. Miles left 2.40 on his bench, 97.8% efficiency, second best in the league.

LIONS D/ST: MINUS 4.00.

That is the entire game. A defense went negative four and he lost by 5.48. Miles built a trade roster, played it almost perfectly, and is 0-2 with 221.48 points, more than five teams with better records. That is not a fantasy team, that is a Greek tragedy with a kicker.

THE WINNERS

LIAM HUGHES, Mount Olympus. 113.46 over Miles 107.98. Margin 5.48.

DAK PRESCOTT 29.76 and CHRISTIAN McCAFFREY 22.60 did it. HARRISON BUTKER put up 16.00, a problem when your CHIEFS D/ST scores 1.00. TERRANCE FERGUSON went 17.40 on the bench while T.J. HOCKENSON started for 5.90. Left 14.60 behind, won by 5.48, should send Miles a fruit basket. 2-0 and nobody is talking about him.

HARRISON BRAGG, Fort Bragg Confederates. 83.68 over Stephen 62.22. Margin 21.46.

The defending champion is NOT 0-2. Put the pitchforks down. He started PATRICK MAHOMES this time (28.98) after benching him for 21.66 in Week 1. KYLER MURRAY sat on IR all week with the concussion, so that call made itself.

DJ MOORE: MINUS 0.10. Started. Last week Moore went 21.00 on Harrison's bench. TRE TUCKER went 22.90 in street clothes and Harrison left 24.80 behind. Fort Bragg is 1-1 with 149.20 points, dead last in scoring, and the six 2027 picks are still gone. The crown is on but it is crooked.

JOSH P, VancouverPantiesDeJarome. 130.90 over Lucas 102.46. Margin 28.44.

CEEDEE LAMB 35.30, BRANDON AUBREY 17.00, PARKER WASHINGTON 16.80 in the flex, VIKINGS D/ST 16.00 on a 3.86 projection. KYLE PITTS SR.: 2.50, second straight week. He left 38.60 on his bench including DALTON SCHULTZ (26.00, highest bench score in the league) and beat the preseason favorite anyway.

PRESTON SCHNEIDER, The Watermark. 114.52 over Evan 81.68. Margin 32.84.

Won without his quarterback. CALEB WILLIAMS put up 7.72 after 37.26 in Week 1, and Preston still cruised behind JAHMYR GIBBS 23.30, CHRIS OLAVE 22.60, CHASE McLAUGHLIN 16.00 and the RAMS D/ST at 11.00. TYLER SHOUGH went 22.38 on the bench. League-best 280.18 points. Maya had them Tier 3, "bubble." Tommy Mancini spent August mocking the Kayshon Boutte signing. Both should put the keyboard down.

SHREYUS SAXENA, Pluto Shraazinatorz. 125.92 over Andrew 82.16. Margin 43.76.

JOSH ALLEN: 40.82, second straight week roughly doubling his projection. JAKE FERGUSON went 20.30 after 2.60 in Week 1. CAMERON DICKER: 1.00, still the worst starter on a winning roster. Left 0.90 on the bench for 99.3% efficiency, best mark by anybody in any week this season.

DREW FLYNN, Englewood Ninjas. 156.48 over Carter 106.40. Margin 50.08.

JAXON SMITH-NJIGBA: 42.50 on an 18.49 projection. JONATHAN TAYLOR 29.20, BROCK PURDY 28.48, JAYLEN WADDLE 21.80 after going 1.20 in Week 1. Four starters over 21. Drew has beaten the defending champion and a Tier 1 roster in consecutive weeks.

MATT GINGRICH, Doob's Agency. 167.68 over Zach 78.50. Margin 89.18.

He started Christian Watson. HE STARTED CHRISTIAN WATSON. I dedicated a Dick of the Day and two columns to this man benching Watson, he finally did it, and Watson went 14.10, the least important number in this recap.

DAVANTE ADAMS: 39.50 IN THE FLEX. JARED GOFF: 29.78. KENNETH WALKER III: 23.80. PATRIOTS D/ST: 20.00. SAQUON BARKLEY went 3.00 on a 17.62 projection and Matt won by 89 anyway. The luckiest 1-0 in the league is now the scariest 2-0.

WEEKLY AWARDS

PLAYER OF THE WEEK: JAXON SMITH-NJIGBA, 42.50. Projected 18.49, more than doubled it, highest score by any player on any roster, started or benched.

BUST OF THE WEEK: JAXSON DART, 0.80 against 18.18. A 17.38-point crater from a starting quarterback. Dishonorable mention to SAQUON BARKLEY (3.00 on 17.62) and BIJAN ROBINSON (11.10 on 22.93).

MANAGER OF THE WEEK: MATT GINGRICH. League-high 167.68, 97.6% of his ceiling, an 89-point win, and he finally started the guys I have been screaming about. Honorable mention to SHREYUS SAXENA at 99.3%.

CLOWN OF THE WEEK: STEPHEN CERQUONE. Bryce Young scored 24.08 on his bench one week after scoring 31.44 on his bench. Fifty-five points of quarterback, two weeks, zero starts, and he lost by 21.46 while leaving 32.46 behind. Dishonorable mention: EVAN BROCKWAY and CARTER COLE, who benched Stefon Diggs again.

BLOWOUT OF THE WEEK: Matt 167.68 over Zach 78.50. Margin 89.18.

NAIL BITER OF THE WEEK: Liam 113.46 over Miles 107.98. Margin 5.48, decided by a defense that scored MINUS 4.00.

STAT LINE OF THE WEEK: DJ MOORE, MINUS 0.10, started by Harrison Bragg one week after Moore scored 21.00 on his bench. He benched the good version and started the version that owes him money. Second straight week the defending champion started a player who finished in the red.

The West has four 2-0 teams and the four highest-scoring rosters in the league. Four of the five 0-2 teams live in the East.

STORYLINES TO TRACK

HARRISON IS 1-1, NOT 0-2. The doomsday column does not get written this week. But 149.20 points is dead last by 6.34, he left 24.80 on the bench, and he started a receiver who finished negative. The six traded picks are still gone and he is winning ugly against 0-2 teams.

FIVE TEAMS ARE 0-2. Stephen, Zach, Evan, Carter and Miles. In a 14-week season that is survivable, and the tell is points. Miles at 221.48 and Evan at 181.94 with a 123-point ceiling are unlucky. Stephen at 155.04 and Zach at 200.80 with a quarterback room on fire are not unlucky, they are bad.

THE BOMBERS ARE FRAUDS AT 1-1 AND THEY KNOW IT. Rick's best-backfield-ever went 21.40 combined. Worst efficiency in the league, and they left more on the bench than they lost by.

MILES AND THE TRADE ROSTER. Everybody wanted to know if the trade-built team would work. It has scored 221.48 in two weeks, third most in the East, and it is 0-2. The roster works. The schedule is a war crime.

THE PREDICTION DESK. EARL HUTCHINSON went 6/7, the best week anybody has had this season. RICO DELGADO went 4/7 but hit a lone wolf for the bonus and 7 total, the week's high score. Season: Earl and Rico tied at 11, Earl ahead on percentage at 11/14. Priya and Marcus 8, Gerald 7, Destiny 6, Sandy 5, Vinny 4. No perfect weeks yet.

AND ME. I went 1 for 7. I picked Stephen over Harrison, Carter over Drew, Andrew over Shreyus, Zach over Matt, and Lucas over Josh P. The only thing I got right was Preston. I said Miles wins if he benches Stafford. He started Stafford, Stafford went 26.98, and he lost anyway. Take the opposite of my picks. Frame this paragraph.

LOOKING AHEAD: WEEK 3

PLUTO SHRAAZINATORZ (2-0, 260.58) at DOOB'S AGENCY (2-0, 274.74). Best matchup of the week and it is not close. Two undefeated rosters, Josh Allen (40.82) against Jared Goff (29.78) and a Davante Adams who just went 39.50 out of a flex. Shreyus needs Dicker (1.00) to look like a kicker. PICK: Matt, because 167.68 with Barkley contributing nothing is terrifying.

THE WATERMARK (2-0, 280.18) at AMON RA DAWGIN (1-1, 219.86). Andrew needs Jefferson (8.50) and Lawrence (6.16) to remember their jobs. Preston needs Caleb Williams to pick a lane after 37.26 and 7.72. PICK: Preston, though Andrew is one Jefferson explosion from flipping it.

ENGLEWOOD NINJAS (2-0, 254.78) at PAVEL DOROFEYEV (0-2, 221.48). Must-win for Miles and the cruelest draw available. Miles needs St. Brown (35.20) and Stafford (26.98) to repeat and that Lions defense nowhere near his lineup. PICK: Drew, and if Miles goes 0-3 with this roster somebody should check on him.

PAKISTAN BOMBERS (1-1, 241.88) at CHICAGO ZESTIEST MAN (0-2, 200.80). Lucas needs Bijan and Jeanty to be the guys Rick promised. Zach needs any quarterback at all after Dart's 0.80. PICK: Lucas, and if the Bombers lose to an 0-2 roster the crown talk ends permanently.

THE VILE HORRENDOUS (0-2, 181.94) at FORT BRAGG (1-1, 149.20). Evan has the better roster, the worse record, and 85.70 left on his bench across two weeks. Harrison has the worst point total in the league. If Evan starts Kelce (25.10) and gets anything from Herbert (7.88) he wins by 20. PICK: Evan, must-win before 0-3 buries him.

I HEART GINGERS (0-2, 193.68) at VANCOUVERPANTIESDEJAROME (1-1, 207.76). Carter needs Stevenson (3.60) and Dobbins (3.60) to produce a pulse. Josh P needs Pitts (2.50) benched into the sun and Schultz (26.00) in the lineup. PICK: Carter, because Chase and Diggs starting the same week finally beats somebody.

STARVING ETHIOPIANS (0-2, 155.04) at MOUNT OLYMPUS (2-0, 218.56). Stephen has scored 92.82 and 62.22 with 55.52 points of Bryce Young on his bench. Liam has won two straight and nobody has noticed. PICK: Liam, unless Stephen starts Young, in which case PICK: Liam anyway.

Two weeks in, the West owns the top four scores, five teams are 0-2, and the defending champion is last in points at 1-1. This league left 261.42 points on the bench and three of the seven losers lost by less than they left behind. Set your damn lineups. Ask Stephen what two weeks of Bryce Young in a polo shirt buys you.

headline: Fawcett Now Owns Three Keeper Picks. Three Teams Own None.
body:
Three trades in forty-eight hours moved thirteen 2027 draft picks and four receivers. When it was over, one manager owned three Keeper round picks and three teams owned none.

It started with Stephen Cerquone. The Starving Ethiopians sent their 2027 Keeper round pick and their 4th to Pakistan Bombers and got back a 3rd, a 6th, a 10th and Mack Hollins. Before the league had finished arguing about it, Zach Ehrig made the same trade from the other side of the standings: Tank Dell, Chicago's Keeper pick, a 6th and a 10th to Lucas Fawcett for a 2nd and an 8th. Then Harrison Bragg and Matt Gingrich closed the week out, Fort Bragg sending its Keeper pick, a 10th and Davante Adams to Doob's Agency for Doob's own 2nd and Deebo Samuel Sr.

Two of those three deals ended in the same driveway. Pakistan Bombers started the week holding one Keeper round pick, the same as everybody else, and finished holding three. In a keeper league the Keeper round is the first round. The third deal was quieter and may be the sharpest anybody made.

"Let me count them, because everybody is describing this week and nobody is adding it up," said Maya Chen. "There are fourteen Keeper round picks in the 2027 draft. Lucas Fawcett holds three: his own, Stephen's and Zach's. Matt Gingrich holds two: his own and Harrison's. Nine managers hold one. Three hold zero, and those three are Fort Bragg, Chicago Zestiest Man and the Starving Ethiopians. Every Keeper pick that moved this week moved toward a team already better than the one selling it."

Rick "The Hammer" Dalton did not need a spreadsheet. "Let me be absolutely clear about what just happened," he said. "Fawcett walked into two rooms this week and walked out of both holding the best asset on the table. He bought the top of two other men's drafts with a 2nd, a 3rd, a 6th, an 8th and a 10th, picks he was never going to use, and threw in Mack Hollins as a tip. Three first round picks in a fourteen team keeper league, on the same roster as Hurts, Jeanty, Robinson, Nacua and McBride. I have been wrong before. Not often. I am not wrong here. This league had a year to stop him and it financed him instead. That's not a prediction, that's a promise."

The shape of his board says the same thing. Fourteen picks with a crater in the middle: three Keepers, then nothing until a 4th. "He sold every pick a normal manager uses for depth and kept only the ones worth a player," Maya said. "That is not hoarding. This is sorted."

Claire Westbrook was more interested in what each seller thought he was buying. "Cerquone is 0-2 and has scored 155.04, second fewest in the league. He does not have a 2027 problem, he has a right now problem, and he turned an asset he cannot use this season into three picks and a body. That is coherent. It is also a total surrender of the one thing that would have made 2027 different, to the manager who beat him by 46 in Week 1."

"Ehrig is the harder case," she went on. "He is genuinely accumulating: sixteen picks, tied for the most in the league, including two 2nds, two 3rds and three 5ths. But this is the third straight time he has sold the scarcest thing on his roster for volume. Drake London in the offseason. Trey McBride last week. His Keeper pick now. A rebuild that trades scarcity for quantity ends with the deepest roster nobody fears."

DeShawn "Showtime" Harris stopped being analytical around the second trade. "THREE KEEPER PICKS! Does anybody in this league own a PHONE?! Stephen is 0-2 and he sold the front of his draft to the man who already beat him by 46! And then ZACH DID IT TOO! THE SAME DAY! And these two are PLAYING EACH OTHER THIS WEEK! Thirteen managers watched this happen live and not ONE called Stephen with a better offer! You are not being beaten, you are being SERVED. SHOWTIME'S SPICY TAKE: Fawcett owns the best roster in this league and now the top of the next draft, and the thirteen of you who allowed it do not get to complain in February. AND I SAID WHAT I SAID."

The other number worth staring at belongs to Fort Bragg. "They hold nine picks for 2027," Maya said. "The next lowest team holds thirteen. Eight of Fort Bragg's own fourteen are sitting on other people's boards: the Keeper, a 2nd and a 10th at Doob's, a 6th and an 11th at The Vile Horrendous, a 3rd and a 5th at Chicago, a 7th at Beer. Three of the nine they still own are borrowed. They are 1-1 with 149.20 points, fewest in the league, and nothing behind it."

Which is what makes the Adams trade the one Claire wanted to sit with. "Bragg needed to win now, so judge it on this season alone and it is defensible. It has not aged well. Adams went 39.50 out of Gingrich's flex in Week 2 and Doob's put up a league-high 167.68 the same afternoon. Look across the table. Gingrich gave up exactly one pick, his own 2nd, and received a starting receiver, a 10th and a Keeper round pick. He is 2-0, he has scored 274.74, and he holds two of the fourteen first round picks in this league. Claire's Verdict: that third trade was Gingrich buying something that should never have been for sale, and it is the best deal of the week by a distance."

Tommy "T-Bone" Mancini filed his from a safe distance. "Fort Bragg's draft board is nine picks deep and I have seen wedding registries with more inventory. Harrison's draft is going to end before the pizza arrives. As for Lucas, he is not managing a fantasy team anymore, he is running a commodities desk. Keeper picks in, mid rounders out, a receiver tossed on the scale to balance the ticket. And a note for the record, because somebody has to keep one. The Watermark still holds all fourteen of its own 2027 picks, every line marked Own. Three trades in two days and Preston Schneider did not look up."

Valentina Rojas closed the desk out. "There is a version of this week that reads as a market working exactly as designed. Managers who cannot win in 2026 sold what they could not use, and managers who can win bought it. That is how a league breathes.

"Then there is the ledger. Cerquone sold his first round pick and his season was already finished. Ehrig sold his for a 2nd he will spend on somebody's fourth receiver. Bragg sold his for a wideout he will start eleven times. Three men gave away the one asset that cannot be replaced, and two of them mailed it to the same address.

"The Bombers and the Zestiest Man play each other this week. One of them just sold the other a first round pick. Whatever the scoreboard says, the receipt was written first. The league remembers."
